Code: dlm/disklock.c mxfs_disklock_recovery_fence_intent (no epoch predicate before desc.victim_epoch = cur->epoch), mxfs_disklock_recovery_slot_status (the predicate that exists elsewhere), dlm/v5_mount.c v5_pr_fence_prove_locked switch (no SUPERSEDED arm before 0.61.2).
defects.mechanism: PROVEN from code + the chain 61 capture. dlm/disklock.c mxfs_disklock_recovery_fence_intent: the no-descriptor path (cur->flags ACTIVE/WITHDRAWN, cur->node_id==victim, !hb_gen_foreign, inc_valid(cur->epoch)) proceeds straight to want->recov.desc.victim_epoch = cur->epoch; there is no inc_eq(cur->epoch, victim_epoch) predicate. The monitor's epoch-change arm (disklock.c ~2757) declares the CACHED incarnation E1 dead and dispatches v5_pr_fence_prove(dead_node, slot, E1); prove_locked freezes the victim key for E1 (mxfs_disklock_victim_key) and calls fence_intent, which lays FENCING with victim_epoch=E2 (the sector's value). On chain 61 that is the GUARD at t+0.5 s. The same classifier that the completion path uses (mxfs_disklock_recovery_slot_status ~8285: ACTIVE + feature block OK + both incarnations nonzero + differing => SUPERSEDED, else FOREIGN) is absent from the intent path. The descriptor-present arm (6749) then returns -ESTALE with no log line for every subsequent prover asked for E1, and the caller's P238-FENCE-NOINTENT line cannot name the standing tuple. Reachability outside a forged sector: node_id is a random UUID hash per mount (dlm/mount.c:144), so a same-node_id later incarnation requires the claim pass-1 own-stamp reclaim (sess89: unreachable by construction) or a foreign/torn writer; the E1-vs-E2 mismatch class itself (any writer changing the epoch of a record the survivors are tracking) is exactly what D-MONITOR-INCARNATION-DOWNGRADE-TO-ZERO's probe exists to exercise.
defects.containment: None. On a production build the trigger needs a same-node_id incarnation change on a tracked slot (foreign/torn writer, or the unreachable own-stamp reclaim); the consequence when it fires is a slot frozen at GUARD with the declared incarnation's recovery never completing.

defects.summary: A node that crashes and remounts before any survivor replayed it (PASS-1 reclaim of its own still-ACTIVE heartbeat stamp) recovers its own dirty journal slice as a trusted XFS log. Every shared metadata block it held at death that was last written by ANOTHER node's slice carries that slice's LSN stamp; whenever that stamp is numerically >= the reclaiming node's transaction LSN the buffer image is silently dropped by the upstream on-disk-LSN skip, exactly the D-0517 mechanism (AGI/inobt/finobt images lost while the changecount-gated inode items apply), while the node's own grants were still held so no other writer could have refreshed the block. Result: half-applied transactions on the node's own crash recovery (inobt allocated + unlinked bucket populated + FREE core, or any AG/dir/bmap-block lost update) with no diagnostic. Per-node slices have independent cycle/block numbering, so the comparison is meaningless on a clustered mount regardless of which path replays the slice.
defects.evidence: Code: xfs/xfs_log.c:642-698 (routing: PASS-1 reclaim 'keeps full recovery'); xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:45227-45242 (adopted_slice_full_replay comment: 'A PASS-1 own-stamp reclaim (nobody replayed us) always performs full recovery'); pal/linux/xfs_super.c:3950-3959; pal/linux/xfs_buf_item_recover.c:1089-1124 (0.61.2 numbering; the unconditional skip); xfs/xfs_inode_item_recover.c:397-440 (trusted path falls back to the di_lsn compare). Measurement of the identical mechanism on the foreign path: D-0517 chain 80 laps 2 and 3 (tests/evidence/sess456_d0517lab_s456b/lap2, lap3) — see that record's SESS459 entry.
defects.mechanism: CODE-PROVEN, NOT YET MEASURED. (1) pal/linux/xfs_super.c:3953 sets m_mxfs_slice_adopted from mxfs_v5_dlm_slice_adopted (pass-2 fresh claim only); a PASS-1 reclaim leaves it false and m_mxfs_bootstrap_adopted false, so xfs_log.c:656-698 sets neither XLOG_MXFS_BOOTSTRAP_ADOPTED nor XLOG_MXFS_ADOPTED_SLICE and xlog_is_mxfs_untrusted_replay() is false for the whole recovery. (2) xlog_recover_commit_trans's authority loop (xfs/xfs_log_recover.c ~3760-3840, mxfs_report_replay_authority) therefore never runs; no ri_mxfs_verdict, no manifest, no live CAW check. (3) xlog_recover_buf_commit_pass2 then reaches the upstream test 'lsn = xlog_recover_get_buf_lsn(); if (lsn != -1 && XFS_LSN_CMP(lsn, current_lsn) >= 0) skip' for every AGF/AGFL/AGI/btree/dir/da/symlink/SB image; the stamp is whichever slice last flushed the block (D-0517 chain 80 lap 2: AG 6 inobt stamped 0x100001183 by slice 31 while slice 6 replayed 0x100000e48/e4c). (4) The inode-item path (xfs/xfs_inode_item_recover.c:397-440) only uses the changecount gate under xlog_is_mxfs_untrusted_replay(); on this trusted path it too falls back to the upstream di_lsn compare (line 435, '> 0'), so inode images are ALSO exposed to the cross-slice veto here. Trigger: the crashed node held resource R at death; R's blocks were last flushed by a predecessor tenure whose slice position is numerically higher than the crashed node's dirty txn LSNs; the node remounts before fencing/foreign replay (fast reboot inside the death-detection window, or a whole-cluster crash where non-bootstrap nodes reclaim their own stamps in PASS-1).
defects.containment: None on a production build: any own-crash recovery that beats the survivors' death detection takes this path. The survivors' foreign replay (once fixed under D-0517) covers only the case where the node stays down long enough to be fenced.
defects.found: sess459 code audit prompted by the D-0517 root (RULE: CONSULT ANOTHER MODEL WHEN STUCK ruling docs/rulings/d0517-buf-lsn-skip-bypass-stop-ship-6-items.md, required change 6): xfs/xfs_log.c:642-698 routes only BOOTSTRAP_ADOPTED and ADOPTED_SLICE (pass-2 fresh claim) mounts through untrusted replay; a PASS-1 own-stamp reclaim ('our own ACTIVE stamp survived — nobody replayed us', xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:45232 'always performs full recovery') replays the dirty own slice as a TRUSTED log: no authority-token evaluation, and pal/linux/xfs_buf_item_recover.c xlog_recover_buf_commit_pass2 applies the upstream 'on-disk LSN >= txn LSN => skip' veto.

Also note for D-0517: because of this, every reachable dirty-slice replay today is untrusted (foreign / adopted / bootstrap-adopted), so the 0.61.4 class-gated bypass covers every path that can execute. The inode path's changecount gate must run on this path too. Never disable the compare globally. 3) Verify with the reclaim reproducer (chk clean, zero SKIP, OVERRIDE-APPLY > 0) plus the whole-cluster-crash restart harness (tests for D-437) with shared-AG churn before the crash. 4) This record blocks D-0517 closure only in the sense that the same mechanism must be closed on both replay paths; D-0517's fix is scoped to the untrusted path and is verified independently. ===== 2026-09-28 (4-node release adjudication): impact set to noblock from this record's own SESS459 reachability measurement, re-checked on the current tree (grep node_uuid_path: only the declaration and the read remain). defects.summary: On a volume whose slice count equals the cluster size, a node that died and reboots CANNOT mount while a survivor holds the transient unclaimed-bucket sweep guard on the dead node's own slot: the claim path counts the table (31 ACTIVE + 1 sweep guard = 32), finds no free slot, and the mount fails immediately with -28 (P300-CLAIM-EXHAUSTED / P300-CLAIM-WITHDRAWN 'retry the mount from a mounted peer's cluster'). The only blocker is a self-clearing transient held by a live peer, yet the mount does not wait for it — the rejoining node's mount unit fails and an operator (or a retry loop) must re-issue the mount after the sweep finishes. The permanent variant (a QUARANTINED verdict occupying the slot) is D-QUARANTINED-SLOT-EXHAUSTS-CLUSTER-ADMISSION-376; this record is the TRANSIENT variant, which the 376 design explicitly classifies as 'retry the mount' rather than 'wait'.

RELOAD-SWEEP bogus_imode=0 zombie_adopt=0 iops_rewire=0 nodes_missing=0 — no other fault in the arm.
defects.mechanism: PROVEN from the kernel log of the failing mount (test2 journalctl -k, 2026-09-02 07:22:53-07:22:57Z): 'P300-CLAIM-EXHAUSTED no free heartbeat slot in 0..31 — this volume has 32 log slices ... Table: 31 live member(s), 0 quarantined recovery verdict(s), 0 withdrawn slice(s) awaiting replay, 0 recovery lease(s) in progress, 1 bucket-sweep guard(s), 0 other, 0 unreadable (plus 0 bucket-sweep guard(s) above the slice count, which are normal).' then 'P300-CLAIM-WITHDRAWN 0 slot(s) hold a dirty WITHDRAWN slice ... 1 hold a transient bucket-sweep guard. A LIVE PEER resolves them ... retry the mount' then 'disklock claim_slot failed: -28' then 'XFS (dm-1): MXFS DLM init failed — aborting mount of cluster (envelope) volume'. The guard was test1's P99-UBSWEEP-HOLD on slot 13 (the victim's own former slot), held 180 s by the arm's ubsweep_hold_ms knob (the artificial hold exposes a window that exists on every real sweep). Code: dlm/disklock.c hb_report_claim_exhausted (~9457) is diagnostic only ('this changes no claim decision'); the claim loop returns -ENOSPC on the first full scan with no retry when the occupants include a transient guard. Contrast: the same node's cleanup remount six seconds after the knob was cleared (07:23:02-07:23:10Z) claimed slot 13 and mounted ('DLM initialized (CAW, slot=13, node_id=2089036436)', 'MXFS mount recovery barrier complete').
defects.containment: Fail-closed and loud: the mount aborts with an explicit -28 and a message that names the transient guard and says to retry; no slot is double-claimed and the guarded slot is never taken while the guard is live (the safety half of the joiner arm held). Cost: a rebooted node at cluster capacity cannot rejoin during any peer's sweep of its old bucket without an external retry.

defects.mechanism: UNKNOWN - no positive attribution is available and none is being asserted. What the evidence RULES OUT: (a) the three known SCST memory-safety defects - all are fixed in the installed build (scst 3.11.0-pre+caw-abort-reclaim.5, srcversion 49601BF23C0AF27910B7E2C; scst_pres.c:2634-2665 carries the .4 signed/offset bound with min(buffer_size, cmd->bufflen); .5 carries the PR-abort tryget), and every one of them announced itself with a loud oops/BUG carrying an SCST frame, which this event did not; (b) the PR READ FULL STATUS overflow specifically - its precursor 'Too big response data len' never appeared and the kmsg guard ran the whole boot without a single halt, precursor or flood trip; (c) the GPU PCIe P2P cause of the 09-01 pair - boot -1 has ZERO nv_dma_map_peer lines and ZERO Xid errors (boot -2, which crashed on it, has 12 and 8 respectively); (d) OOM / page-allocation failure - none in boot -1; (e) filesystem-headroom wedge - / at 85% used, 273G free, inside the preflight floor; (f) log flood - peak 1303 kernel lines/min vs the 182 lines/s wedge class. What it leaves: a fault that never reached the kernel's own oops path - a triple fault (corrupted page tables / IDT / CR3), or a hardware-initiated reset. Both are consistent with the host running with the IOMMU DISABLED (/proc/cmdline: iommu=off intel_iommu=off intremap=off) alongside 3-4 CUDA GPUs, out-of-tree vmmon/vmnet/vboxdrv, an out-of-tree SCST target and 32 KVM guests: any device can DMA anywhere in physical memory with no protection and no fault reporting to name the offender.
defects.containment: None applied. The rig is currently DOWN of its own accord (0 VMs running, scst not loaded, no run.sh) following the reset; no halt flag was set because nothing detected a crash. NOTE: mxfs-crash-latch.service cannot latch on this failure mode - it keys on a pstore record, and this event produced none, so the rig was free to restart into the same conditions. That gap is itself part of this defect.

defects.next: This defect CANNOT be root-caused with the instrumentation the host currently has - that is the first thing to fix, and it is the blocking step. The host has NO surviving evidence channel for a fault that does not reach the oops path: (1) no BMC - ipmi_si is not loaded and SMBIOS type 38 (IPMI Device Information) is absent, so the ASMB card is not present or not enabled in BIOS; there is no SEL to read and installing ipmitool alone would not create one. (2) no netconsole (not loaded, no modprobe.d config) - the only channel that survives a hard lockup or triple fault. (3) no kdump - crashkernel= absent from /proc/cmdline, kdump-tools inactive, /var/crash empty. (4) no metrics - sysstat is installed and its cron fires every 10 min but /etc/default/sysstat has ENABLED="false" and /var/log/sysstat is empty, so there is no CPU/memory/IO history across the event. (5) kernel.hardlockup_panic=0 and kernel.softlockup_panic=0, so a lockup prints rather than producing a recorded panic. ACTIONS, in order: [a] enable sysstat collection (no reboot, zero risk); [b] configure netconsole to another host on 192.168.1.x/192.168.120.x (no reboot); [c] decide on crashkernel= and, separately, on restoring the IOMMU in at least a fault-reporting mode - BOTH need a kernel-cmdline change and therefore a reboot, which per RULE: NEVER REBOOT THE LAB HOST only the user may perform, and the iommu=off is presumed deliberate (GPU P2P / passthrough) so it is a user decision with a real trade-off, not a defect to be silently fixed. Until at least [b] lands, a recurrence will again leave nothing. ===== RECURRENCES (read 2026-10-16 from journalctl --list-boots, last -x -F, /var/lib/systemd/pstore): the same silent end - no shutdown, no ERST record, no mce at next boot - on 2026-09-17 14:19, 16:53, 18:36 CDT; 09-21 14:30; 10-07 06:47; 10-15 15:42 (back 15:58; serv 192.168.1.5 also rebooted ~15:50); 10-16 between 12:04:10 and 12:05:30 (the journal ends 12:03:32 but rig evidence files on / carry mtimes and a recorded action at 12:04:10, so the journal tail was simply unflushed). Most return in 2-3 min (immediate reset, BIOS POST). Workload at each varied: Sep 17 x3 and Sep 21 near idle (9-65 journal lines in the last 2 min, no SCST, no vLLM, no rig evidence written); 10-15 vLLM serving on the 4 RTX 3090s, no rig; 10-16 the 8/net/mesh/mpath board had just set test14's path a down (virsh domif-setlink) and vLLM was stopped since 09:53. sysstat now records (action [a] done): 10-16 12:03:01 load 8.28 on 56 CPUs, 66 GB available, no OOM, root 197 GB free. EDAC mc0-mc3 ce/ue 0, zero mce/Hardware Error/throttle lines in boots -8..0. Still no netconsole, no BMC (no /dev/ipmi0), no kdump, no UPS logging: action [b] is still the blocking step. Hardware below the kernel (PSU under 4 GPUs, mains/UPS, board/BIOS 4301 of 2020) fits every recurrence; the rig is not common to them. ===== ===== RECURRENCE 2026-10-16 ~21:09 CDT (boot 5dd7bd8d893e456aa9b8f719baccf362, 12:05:31 to 21:08:39 by the journal): the same silent end. boot -1 has no shutdown sequence (no systemd-shutdown / shutdown or reboot target line; last -x -F ends every session of that boot in 'crash'), /sys/fs/pstore empty at the next boot (systemd-pstore skipped on ConditionDirectoryNotEmpty), no new /var/lib/systemd/pstore dir (newest 7680563026138759178, 2026-09-01 08:48), EDAC mc0-mc3 ce_count/ue_count 0, no mce/machine check/Hardware Error line in boot 0. Bracket: alive at 21:09:02 (tests/evidence/netconsole.log mtime: the host listener received a guest datagram), the journal ends 21:08:39 (a vLLM log line; last kernel line 21:08:04, an SCST Reservation conflict), a Claude session transcript (81d1c9bd) was last written ~21:09; boot 0 kernel 21:18:16, so the host was gone ~9 min, longer than the 2-3 min returns before. Workload at the end: vLLM serving gemma-4-31B on the 4 GPUs with live requests (836 tokens/s prompt at 21:08:19), and the rig in one tests/mpath/fenced_held_unmount.sh control lap on g2b (fhu_ab a4 lap 1: test16 frozen 21:08:38, test15 PREEMPT AND ABORT of test16's key 21:08:43, thaw, writer killed 21:08:44, then 2 s ssh polls of test16's path in-flight counts). defects.summary: After a whole-cluster bootstrap the lone survivor's post-recovery ORPHAN SCAN (mxfs_orphan_scan, run after every dead-slot bucket sweep) xfs_iget()s a zombie that IS a member of a not-yet-swept slot bucket (the unclaimed previous-incarnation slot's bucket), finds it 'bucketed' and merely xfs_irele()s it WITHOUT loading its unlinked-chain state (no xfs_inode_reload_unlinked_bucket, no i_unlinked_bucket stamp). The irele queues inodegc; xfs_inactive -> xfs_inactive_ifree -> xfs_ifree -> xfs_iunlink_remove_inode runs with i_prev_unlinked=0 and i_unlinked_bucket=-1, so it computes the LEGACY bucket agino%64 (bucket 4) while the on-disk membership is in the slot bucket (bucket 1); bucket 4's head is NULLAGINO, xfs_verify_agino fails, P71-INSTR agi-unlinked-garbage -> XFS_CORRUPTION_ERROR -> xfs_ifree -117 -> force shutdown -> P-SESSION-POISON. The multi-node fail-closed guards that would have caught the unstamped remove (mxfs_ifree_unlinked_preflight P-UNLPRE-NOBUCKET -EAGAIN, P84, P85) were all DISABLED because the survivor was in dlm_caw single_node=true (sole live member after the bootstrap), so legacy hashing was used against a slot-partitioned on-disk list. Meanwhile the legitimate sweeper of that bucket (P99-UBSWEEP slot=1) could not take the inode (xfs_iget -> -ENOENT: NEED_INACTIVE with nlink 0 cannot be re-grabbed) and 'stays pending'. Net: one rm'd open file + whole-cluster death = the recovering node shuts down (fail-closed, but the cluster's only member is now poisoned).

defects.mechanism: (1) xfs_icreate -> xfs_inode_init installs only xfs_setup_inode; the i_op/i_fop tables come from xfs_setup_iops, which xfs_generic_create calls itself before d_instantiate. mxfs_dirshard_alloc_parent / alloc_container called xfs_finish_inode_setup without it, so the creator's in-core parent kept the VFS empty_iops; d_flags_for_inode() typed the dentry DCACHE_AUTODIR_TYPE (S_IFDIR with no ->lookup) and walk_component/O_DIRECTORY return -ENOTDIR. The peer igets the parent from disk via xfs_setup_existing_inode, so only the creator is affected (explains cc lap 1 FAIL / laps 2-3 PASS). (2) mxfs_dirshard_iget used XFS_IGET_UNTRUSTED; xfs_imap_lookup answers it from xfs_ialloc_read_agi(pag, NULL) + an inobt lookup taken WITHOUT the AG DLM lock — the peer's cached AGI/inobt image predates the creator's dialloc of the holder/containers, so 'untrusted and free' -> -EINVAL (xfs/libxfs/xfs_ialloc.c xfs_imap_lookup). mxfs_dirshard_free_container listed -EINVAL among the 'already freed' errnos and cleared the bit. (3) xfs_readdir asserts XFS_IOLOCK_SHARED|EXCL on the directory it reads; iterate_dir holds the PARENT's i_rwsem, a container has no dentry and nobody takes its i_rwsem. The consumer_refresh + i_dlm_stale settle in xfs_file_readdir run on the parent (no entries) and the container's peer-armed reload can only fire inside xfs_readdir under mxfs_dirshard_readdir's own ILOCK_SHARED, where mxfs_dlm_reload_inode must bail.

defects.summary: On MXFS an XFS_IGET_UNTRUSTED iget decides 'is this inode number allocated?' from xfs_imap_lookup, which reads the AGI and walks the inobt via xfs_ialloc_read_agi(pag, NULL, ...) with NO AG DLM lock — i.e. from whatever AGI/inobt buffers this node last cached. A peer's allocation of the number is invisible until this node next acquires that AG, so a valid reference to a peer-created inode reads as FREE (-EINVAL) or NOT-IN-ANY-CHUNK (-EINVAL) for an unbounded time. Callers: pal/linux/xfs_export.c xfs_nfs_get_inode (NFS / open_by_handle_at -> ESTALE for peer-created files), xfs/xfs_itable.c bulkstat/inumbers (peer-created inodes silently skipped: 'if (error == -ENOENT || error == -EINVAL) goto out_advance'), xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:36527 P88-REAP-RETRY (an -EINVAL retires the reap entry as 'freed elsewhere / vanished'), xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:51864 orphan scan (iget AFTER the AG lock is dropped), xfs/xfs_zone_gc.c, xfs/xfs_inode.c:6083 xfs_iunlink_reload_next (already under the AG lock — coherent), xfs/xfs_mount.c rootino (mount time — coherent).
defects.evidence: Code: xfs/libxfs/xfs_ialloc.c xfs_imap_lookup (three -EINVAL arms, now named by P-IMAP-UNTRUSTED-FREE / P-IMAP-UNTRUSTED-NOREC probes, 0.64.11+); call sites above. Observation (via the sharding user): D-0526 evidence — peer -EINVAL on every readdir/lookup/create of a freshly published sharded dir while the creator's own view (post-iops fix) and the platter (chk: containers 133.. allocated, manifest valid) said the inodes existed. Direct measurement pending: tests/d0527_untrusted_iget_peer.sh (handle minted on the creator after 200 allocations, opened by handle on a peer that had cached the AG's inobt through an earlier warm handle open; path lookup alongside as the trusted control) — chain 110 (tests/sess470_chain110_d0527_handle_probe.sh, three node pairings, gated behind chain 109 on 0.64.12).
defects.mechanism: xfs_iget(UNTRUSTED) -> xfs_iget_cache_miss -> xfs_imap(pag, tp=NULL, ino, imap, XFS_IGET_UNTRUSTED) -> xfs_imap_lookup: xfs_ialloc_read_agi(pag, NULL, 0, &agbp) returns the CACHED AGI buffer (no _XBF_FUA_FRESH gate applies without the AG lock), xfs_inobt_lookup walks cached inobt blocks; 'if (!error && i == 0) error = -EINVAL' / 'rec.ir_startino > agino || ... <= agino -> -EINVAL' / '(flags & UNTRUSTED) && (rec.ir_free & mask) -> -EINVAL'. MXFS refreshes AG buffers on mxfs_ag_dlm_lock acquisition (Invariant 1 drain on the releaser, FUA-fresh reads on the acquirer); nothing on this path takes it. The trusted path does not consult the inobt at all (arithmetic imap + the inode DLM-coherent cluster read + P-IGET-ENOENT arbitration), which is why dirents and the D-0526 fix work.
defects.containment: None. NFS exports / open_by_handle_at of files created on another node can fail ESTALE until the serving node touches the AG; bulkstat omits them; P88 reap-retry entries can be retired on a false 'vanished' (the unlinked bucket remains the durable record, so that case degrades to a delay, not a loss). The dir-sharding user is fixed separately (D-0526, trusted iget).

On the shared directory of the crash_consistency workload: n=15 samples, p50 14.9 ms, p90 52.7 ms, max 97.1 ms. A single COMPARE-AND-WRITE to one 512-byte slot on the shared LUN should cost the storage round trip, order 1 ms. defects.mechanism:
SESS481 THE 9.42 ms/ATTEMPT HEADLINE IS INFLATED — QUOTE 5.41 ms INSTEAD.  Two free analyses over the same 17558 samples, no rig time.  (1) THE RESIDUE IS SUPER-LINEAR IN RETRIES, not proportional.  Bucketing (wall_ms - sleep_ms) by retry count: retries=1 n=10181 resid 10.83 ms (5.41/attempt); =2 n=4053 26.66 (8.89); =3 n=1890 49.95 (12.49); =4 n=839 83.55 (16.71); =5 n=413 108.64 (18.11); =6 n=120 138.91 (19.84); =7 n=44 130.82 (16.35).  A least-squares fit returns a NEGATIVE intercept (-36.2 ms fixed + 22.6 ms/attempt), which is the arithmetic signature of convexity, so the linear "per attempt" model the 9.42 figure assumes is simply the wrong shape.  (2) THE SUPER-LINEARITY IS LARGELY SELECTION, NOT AN ESCALATING CODE PATH.  Counting, per sample, how many other P381 events landed in the SAME SECOND on the SAME node: retries=1 -> 31.5, =2 36.3, =3 43.7, =4 58.0, =5 63.3, =6 63.1.  Local contention roughly DOUBLES from the 1-retry bucket to the 5-retry bucket, tracking the 3.3x rise in per-attempt residue.  An unlock that needs many retries is by construction one occurring inside a heavy burst, when the device queue, the scheduler and every mutex are slower — so the tail measures WHEN those unlocks happen at least as much as what they do.
CONSEQUENCE: use the LEAST-CONTENDED bucket as the per-attempt estimate.  At retries=1 (n=10181) the unaccounted cost is 5.41 ms per attempt, and that bucket carries NO caw_inode_backoff at all (it is skipped below retry 2, dlm/dlm_caw.c:8097).  Against a measured slot round trip of 0.77-1.54 ms that leaves roughly 4 ms per attempt genuinely unexplained at low contention — a real defect, but appreciably smaller and better bounded than the 9.42 ms first recorded.  tools/caw_unlock_audit.py now prints this floor beside the aggregate and says which to quote.
WHAT caw_inode_backoff CAN ACCOUNT FOR, modelled rather than measured: it sleeps rnd % cap with cap = min(4 + 2*retry, 20) (dlm/dlm_caw.c:8112-8118), so expected sleep per call is cap/2 and the cumulative expectation over an unlock with R retries (calls fire at retry 2..R) is R=2 ~4 ms, R=3 ~9, R=4 ~15, R=5 ~22, R=6 ~30, R=7 ~39.  Subtracting that from the observed residues leaves 22.7/41.0/68.6/86.6/108.9 ms — i.e. it explains only about 15-25%, and the remainder is still convex, which the burst-density finding above accounts for.  backoff_ms= (0.65.0) will replace this MODEL with a MEASUREMENT; do not treat the model as the answer. || SESS481 THE find_slot HYPOTHESIS IS WEAKENED BY A STRUCTURAL MEASUREMENT — NOT DEAD, BUT DO NOT BUILD ON IT.  New tool tools/caw_slot_census.py reads the CAW slot table straight out of the SCST backing file (/home/steve/disk.img) on the target host: no rig time, no lock, read-only, cannot disturb a run.  (tools/caw_slotdump cannot do this — it speaks SG_IO and so needs an initiator.)  The base is exact rather than guessed: chk_mxfs reports disklock_offset=67117056 for this LUN, and lock_region_offset = disklock_offset + MXFS_DISKLOCK_HB_SIZE (64 x 512) = 0x400a000, per dlm/dlm_caw.c:15522 and dlm/disklock.h:125-126.  CENSUS ON THE IDLE TABLE (cluster between chains, 2026-09-04): live=99 (66 INODE, 33 AG), TOMBSTONES=0, empty=65437, LOAD FACTOR 0.0015, and 99 of 99 live slots sit at DISPLACEMENT 0 — every resource is at its computed home, so a lookup costs exactly ONE 16-slot span read.  At that load a linear probe cannot be walking chains and the 9.42 ms/attempt residue cannot be span-read I/O.  THE MEASUREMENT'S OWN LIMIT, stated so nobody over-reads it: this is an IDLE table.  The workload creates 3200 files and tombstones are explicitly skip-but-continue (MXFS_CAW_TOMBSTONE_MAGIC "MXDL", dlm/dlm_caw.h:33), so the open question is whether churn accumulates them during a row.  But even a full 3200-slot working set is load factor 0.05, where expected linear-probe displacement is ~0.03 slots, so the hypothesis needs tombstone accumulation of a wholly different order to survive — and zero tombstones on an idle table is evidence they do not persist.  TWO INDEPENDENT INSTRUMENTS NOW SETTLE IT AND THEY CANNOT BE FOOLED THE SAME WAY: find_ms= (direct, in-kernel, 0.65.0) and the census (structural, offline).  Chain 128 runs BOTH and takes the census immediately after each row, BEFORE the next leg's prep re-mkfs's the LUN.  IF BOTH RETURN NULL the residue is neither the backoff ladder, nor the device, nor the probe walk, and the next boundary to instrument is inside the CAS attempt itself (caw_cas_slot and the lreq/publication machinery it calls) — not a fourth guess at the same three suspects.
ALSO CORRECTED, because it nearly caused a duplicate filing: the block comment at dlm/dlm_caw.c:1436 reads as though the span read is still broken and spanning defaulted OFF.  It is not.  That defect was root-caused (the struct had grown while find_slot indexes the span buffer as an array of it, so every slot past the first decoded 8 bytes off), fixed, and closed as D-CAW-CLAIM-RETRY-EXHAUSTION-SHUTDOWN (critical, 2026-08-01); mxfs_caw_probe_span_enable is 1, and sess481 re-verified ZERO P94-SPAN-DISAGREE across all 32 nodes of a full crash_consistency row.  The comment now carries that epilogue. || SESS481 SECOND CORRECTION — TWO NUMBERS BELOW ARE WRONG AND ONE CLAIM IS RETRACTED.  (1) The figures "0.22 ms per slot read (P297-TKT read_ms/reads)" and "0.37 ms per CAW op (P138-AGWAIT caw_svc_ms/reads)" were derived by dividing sum(read_ms) by sum(reads) ACROSS SAMPLES.  That is invalid: dlm/dlm_caw.c:6908 ASSIGNS acq_read_ms = now - t0 on every poll, so read_ms is the LAST read's duration, while reads is CUMULATIVE — a per-iteration value over a cumulative count.  THE CORRECT DIRECT FIGURES, read as the per-read values they are: P297-TKT read_ms mean 0.77 ms, p50 1, p90 2, max 32 (n=3084); P138-AGWAIT caw_svc_ms mean 1.54 ms, p50 1, p90 4, max 37 (n=423).  The CONCLUSION is unchanged and in fact still comfortable — a slot operation costs well under 2 ms against a 9.42 ms residue — but the specific numbers must not be quoted as 0.22/0.37.  (2) RETRACTED: "the same signature appears on the acquire side: ~242 ms per acquire wait unaccounted".  That came from treating P297-TKT's el_ms (cumulative since wait start) against slept_ms and read_ms (both LAST-value — slept_ms prints last_sleep_ms, dlm/dlm_caw.c:6970).  Mixing them proves nothing in either direction, so the acquire side is now UNKNOWN, not anomalous.  A cumulative sleep total already existed as sleep_tot_ms and simply was not printed.
INSTRUMENTATION ADDED 0.65.0 SO THE ACQUIRE SIDE CAN BE ANSWERED: P297-TKT now also carries read_sum_ms= (new accumulator beside the per-read value, which P-ACQ-STUCK still needs) and sleep_sum_ms= (the pre-existing sleep_tot_ms, now printed).  With those a wait's read and sleep TOTALS can be stated rather than inferred.
WHAT STILL STANDS, AND WHY: the UNLOCK-side residue is totals-against-totals and is unaffected by any of the above — p381_sleep_ms ACCUMULATES (dlm/dlm_caw.c:10675 and :11148, both +=) and wall_ms is measured from a single p381_t0 (:10559).  So "17558 contended unlocks, 616.5 s of node-time = 21.4% of the row's 2880 node-seconds, of which 26.5% is counted backoff sleep and 73.5% (9.42 ms/attempt) is UNACCOUNTED" is sound, and the find_slot hash-chain-walk hypothesis for that residue is untouched.
METHOD RULE THIS RECORD NOW CARRIES TWICE: before dividing any probe field by any other, check whether each is CUMULATIVE or LAST-VALUE.  Two separate wrong root causes in one session came from skipping that check — first naming a subtracted residue after an unmeasured mechanism, then dividing a per-iteration value by a cumulative count. || SESS481 SELF-CORRECTION, READ THIS BEFORE THE TWO PARAGRAPHS BELOW: the claim further down that "~74% of the cost is slot I/O service time" and "~9.6 ms per slot round trip" IS REFUTED, by direct probes on the SAME run.  wall_ms minus sleep_ms is not slot I/O; it is UNACCOUNTED, and it was labelled wrongly.  The direct service-time measurements from tests/evidence/run_crash_consistency_20260904T000831Z say a slot round trip is FAST: P297-TKT read_ms=2374 ms over reads=10756 gives 0.22 ms per slot read (n=3084 samples), and P138-AGWAIT caw_svc_ms=651 ms over reads=1754 gives 0.37 ms per CAW op (n=423).  Against a subtraction estimate of 9.42 ms/attempt that means roughly 96% of the non-sleep time in a contended unlock is in NEITHER the counted sleep NOR the device.  The same signature appears on the acquire side: P297-TKT el_ms mean 280.5 ms against slept_ms mean 37.2 and read_ms mean 0.77 — ~242 ms per acquire wait likewise unaccounted.  So the transport is not slow; something inside the CAW protocol's own loops is holding time that no counter sees.
HOST STARVATION IS EXCLUDED as the explanation: clyde has 56 CPUs and the board row recorded hostload=20.26, i.e. ~36% utilisation, so sleep overshoot from CPU oversubscription cannot account for it (30 VMs x 4 vcpu = 120 vcpu over 56 cores is 2.1x allocated but nowhere near saturated at that load).
WHERE IT MUST BE, FROM THE SOURCE: p381_t0 is stamped at dlm/dlm_caw.c:10559, AFTER the clear-window wait (lreq_clr_begin_wait, :10524), so wall_ms brackets only the retry loop.  The loop body contains exactly two unmeasured things: (1) caw_inode_backoff (:10566) sleeps WITHOUT being added to p381_sleep_ms — but it returns early for retry < 2 (dlm/dlm_caw.c:8069) and the MEDIAN unlock has retries=1, so it cannot explain the median gap of wall p50 20 ms against sleep p50 7 ms; (2) find_slot (:10567), which re-walks the resource's hash chain in MXFS_CAW_PROBE_SPAN = 16-slot span reads (dlm/dlm_caw.c:1427-1434) ON EVERY RETRY, even though the retry already holds slot_idx from the previous iteration.  HYPOTHESIS (not yet proven, do not patch on it): the unlock's cost is the repeated hash-chain walk, not the CAS and not the backoff.  If so the fix is cheap and local — a retry re-reads the ONE slot it already located instead of re-walking the chain — but it must be measured first.
INSTRUMENTATION LANDED 0.65.0 (UNBUILT at filing): P381-UNLK-CONTEND now also carries find_ms= and backoff_ms=, bracketing both call sites, so wall = sleep + find + backoff + residue is a closed account.  tools/caw_unlock_audit.py harvests it, prints the residue EXPLICITLY as unaccounted rather than mislabelling it, and refuses to call it slot I/O; it reports find_ms as NOT INSTRUMENTED for pre-0.65.0 logs so an old capture cannot be read as a new one.  Chain 128 (tests/sess481_chain128_create_cost.sh) builds it.
METHOD NOTE for whoever reads this next: the wrong attribution came from dividing a SUBTRACTED residue by attempts and naming the quotient after a mechanism nobody had measured.  A residue is not a measurement of the thing you suspect is in it.  The direct probes that refuted it were already shipping and cost nothing to harvest. || SESS481 CORRECTION TO FIX DIRECTION (b) BELOW, MADE BEFORE ANYONE BUILDS ON IT: the per-field-versioning idea does not work, and the reason is on-disk.  dlm/dlm_caw.h:35 sets MXFS_CAW_SLOT_SIZE = 512 and dlm/dlm_caw.h:321 carries a _Static_assert that sizeof(struct mxfs_caw_lock_slot) == 512 — one slot is EXACTLY ONE SECTOR, which is the granularity of the SCSI COMPARE-AND-WRITE.  The compare therefore covers all 512 bytes, i.e. every peer's waiter bit, not just the single uint32_t generation at dlm_caw.h:152.  Re-versioning fields inside the slot cannot help: any byte a peer writes anywhere in the sector miscompares every other node's in-flight RMW.  The false sharing is at the CAW PRIMITIVE's granularity, not at the struct's.  So (b) is really: SPLIT THE SLOT ACROSS SECTORS — holder state in one sector, waiter registration in another, so a releaser's bit clear and a waiter's registration are no longer the same compare-and-write.  That is an on-disk format change to a structure the architecture pins (the CAW slot table is fixed at 65536 slots on disk), so it needs a format version and a RULE: CONSULT ANOTHER MODEL WHEN STUCK design review before any code.  It is not a reason to prefer (a); the two are independent and (a) is measurable first. || SESS481 MEASURED — THE BACKOFF-LADDER HYPOTHESIS BELOW IS REFUTED; THE COST IS SLOT I/O SERVICE TIME.  The discriminating measurement the next_step asked for already exists in the shipping build: P381-UNLK-CONTEND (dlm/dlm_caw.c:11238, added sess380 for D-32NODE-SHARED-DIR-CREATE-PACE) reports per contended unlock: retries, miscmp, sleep_ms, wall_ms and a full miscompare-cause breakdown.  Harvested from tests/evidence/run_crash_consistency_20260904T000831Z/kernlog_test{1..32}.gz (0.64.37, sv EAD72FC7EC56BA505829901, 32 nodes, one 90 s crash_consistency row) — 17558 contended unlocks fleet-wide:
  retries   sum=30560  mean=1.7  p50=1  p90=3  max=12
  miscmp    sum=30560  mean=1.7  p50=1  p90=3  max=12
  sleep_ms  sum=163349 mean=9.3  p50=7  p90=20 max=94
  wall_ms   sum=616544 mean=35.1 p50=20 p90=78 max=471
  cause: contended=30487 (99.8%), multigen=28879 (94.5%), holders=1605, benign=73, noreg=3, and fast/ident/selfbits/removed/yieldto/control ALL ZERO.
THE SPLIT: mean wall 35.1 ms against mean sleep 9.3 ms leaves ~25.8 ms per unlock that is NOT the backoff ladder.  At mean 1+retries = 2.7 attempts that is ~9.6 ms per attempt, i.e. per slot read-modify-write round trip against the shared LUN.  So the escalating jitter accounts for about 26% of the cost and the remaining ~74% is slot I/O service time.  Removing the ladder — which sess5 proved orphans slot bits and convoys the cluster — could at best recover a quarter of this defect.
FLEET SCALE: 616.5 s of node-time inside contended unlocks against 32 nodes x 90 s = 2880 node-seconds of run, i.e. 21.4% of all node-time in that row is spent inside a contended unlock.
THE MECHANISM THE CAUSE BREAKDOWN NAMES: multigen is 94.5% of miscompares — the slot's generation moved between our read and our compare-and-write.  Every one of 26-28 peers is writing waiter bits into the SAME slot, and one version counter appears to cover the whole slot, so any peer write invalidates every other node's in-flight RMW.  With an RMW window of ~9.6 ms and 26-28 peers mutating, the window is far longer than the inter-arrival time of peer mutations, so miscompare is the normal outcome rather than the exception.  This is false sharing at the slot level, not lock contention: the releaser and the waiters are touching logically disjoint fields.  NOTE selfbits=0 and ident=0 across all 17558 samples — no unlock lost a race to its own bits, and none was a benign identical rewrite.
TWO FIX DIRECTIONS, NEITHER YET RULED: (a) reduce the SERVICE TIME of a slot operation — ~9.6 ms per round trip is 10-50x what the NVMe-backed SCST/iSCSI path should cost, and under this workload the device queue is loaded by the inode-acquire fast poll (mxfs_caw_inode_fastpoll, DEFAULT ON, ~32 slot reads per waiter per wait x 31 waiters against the one hot slot), so the poll storm is a live suspect for inflating the very service time this defect measures; (b) stop the false sharing — if waiter bits and holder bits were separately versioned (or in disjoint sectors), a releaser's bit clear would not miscompare against waiter churn at all, and the retry term would collapse without touching the ladder that sess5's evidence requires.
CONSEQUENCE FOR D-32NODE-SHARED-DIR-CREATE-PACE: sess481's ceiling ruling on that record says lock-HANDOFF tuning cannot make the crash_consistency row pass, and that stands.  But this measurement shows the fastpoll A/B queued there may matter through a different route than the one it was ruled against: not by shortening the handoff, but by unloading the device queue that sets slot-operation service time, which is inside the WORK term.  Read chain 127's result with that in mind. || NOT YET PROVEN -- do not patch on this paragraph. The leading hypothesis is the anti-CAS-storm unlock backoff: mxfs_caw_unlock_backoff (dlm/dlm_caw.c:534) is DEFAULT ON and, on an INODE-unlock CAS miscompare, sleeps a node-phased retry-escalating jitter of 1..~15 ms and keeps retrying (wall-clock bounded rather than count-bounded, dlm/dlm_caw.c:10458-10459) instead of returning -EIO. That behaviour is deliberate and load-bearing -- with it OFF, sess5 measured an unlock losing 100 tight retries against 8-node waiter-bit churn, orphaning the slot bit and convoying every peer 300 s+ on a lock nobody held. So the escalating backoff must NOT simply be removed. Under the crash_consistency workload the releasing node is CAS-ing a slot that 26-28 peers are concurrently writing waiter bits into, so miscompares are the norm rather than the exception and the escalation ladder is climbed on nearly every release. Competing candidates that the measurement does not yet exclude: target-side COMPARE-AND-WRITE emulation cost in SCST, the CAW command queueing behind the fastpoll read traffic of 31 waiters on the same slot (mxfs_caw_inode_fastpoll, DEFAULT ON, adds ~32 slot reads per waiter per wait), forced-unit-access/flush ordering on the CAW command, or scheduling delay before submission.

defects.next: 1) THE DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT, before any patch: instrument the wire unlock to separate software retry from device service time. Count, per unlock: CAS attempts, miscompares, total sleep time in the backoff ladder, and the submit->complete latency of each individual CAW command. If sleep time dominates, the ladder is the cause and the fix is to shorten/replace the escalation (e.g. bounded immediate re-CAS on a miscompare whose delta is only a waiter-bit change -- caw_unlk_delta_is_registration at dlm/dlm_caw.c:10396 already classifies exactly that case, and mxfs_caw_unlock_fastretry / _max=4 / _ms=8 at dlm/dlm_caw.c:223-238 already exist but default OFF). If device service time dominates, the cause is at the target and the fix is elsewhere. 2) In the SAME run collect SCSI opcode / sector-range / queue-depth counts so the fastpoll read traffic on the hot slot can be separated from the CAW traffic. 3) Do NOT disable mxfs_caw_unlock_backoff to make the number look better: sess5 proved that path orphans slot bits and convoys the cluster.

It is a pace defect, and pace is not on the release path. The cluster size is the one the evidence was taken on (32 nodes); it has not been measured on a smaller one.

defects.summary: On the 0.69.2 unmount ordering (AG grants published, then the final SB summary sync and xfs_unmountfs), 23 of 32 nodes that closed 400 unlinked-but-open files and ran umount in the same shell command NEVER RETURNED from umount within the 240 s budget. Every one of the 23 printed P482-UMOUNT-AGREL (the grants were published) at 04:30:12Z and then nothing further that the sweep captured — no P-SB-SEALED, no P483-AGFREE-WINDOW, no P483-AGMETA-AFTER-AGFREE (so no AG-metadata write was issued after publication before the stall). The 9 nodes that completed did so in about one second and had no inactivation left at put_super. The 23 hung nodes were then power-cycled by the next leg's prep, and node journals are volatile, so where they were stuck is UNKNOWN. On 0.69.3 (the D-0483 hoist) the identical workload unmounted 32/32 in 15 s, which is regression evidence for the new ordering and is NOT a disposition of this record: the changed ordering could avoid several unrelated waits.
defects.evidence: tests/evidence/sess485_agfree_hoist_s485a/base/work.txt: 32 nodes report made=400 held=400; 9 report 'RC=0 UNMOUNTED' (test2,5,7,9,13,15,28,31,32); 23 report no rc. base/p483_testN.txt for each of the 23: exactly two lines, P482-UMOUNT-AGREL ags_seen=63 ags_released=1 and P482-AGIFC-AUDIT-COVERAGE calls=1 ran=1, both at 04:30:12; the sweep ran at ~04:34 while the nodes were still hung, so the absence of any later matching line is real for the patterns the filter carried (P483-|P485-|P482-UMOUNT-AGREL|P482-AGIFC-AUDIT-COVERAGE|P-AGIFC-RELEASE-MISMATCH|P-SB-SEAL-|P-SB-SUMMARY-FINAL) — the filter did NOT carry hung-task, P-SB-SUMMARY-LOCK, P6S-ARM-REFUSED or CAW-poll lines, which is why the stall site is unknown. base/chk.txt rc=4 with 404 ERROR lines was taken on a NON-QUIESCENT image (23 mounts still up mid-unmount) and is not a platter verdict. The fix leg on the same harness, same prep, same workload: umount wall 15 s, 32/32 clean, chk 0 errors.
defects.mechanism: SESS487 LAP 3 MEASURED (chain 135 s487a base leg, frozen 0.69.2, 28/32 hung, stacks captured before reboot — tests/evidence/sess485_agfree_hoist_s487a/base/hang_test*.txt, kjournal_test*.txt; prose digest in the sess487 ccmemory): candidate (b) IS the fleet-wide shape and the holder's stall is the AIL. 26/28 umount tasks: state S in caw_nudge_wait <- caw_acquire_poll_sleep <- caw_wait_for_grant <- caw_lock_body <- mxfs_dlm_caw_lock <- mxfs_v5_dlm_inode_lock <- mxfs_sb_summary_lock <- mxfs_sb_summary_final_sync <- xfs_fs_put_super (waiting for the cluster-wide SB summary EX lock); 1/28 (test10) the same chain inside the slot read. 1/28 (test1) — the ONLY node with a P-SB-SUMMARY-LOCK line, i.e. the holder — state D in xfs_ail_push_all_sync <- xfs_log_quiesce <- put_super, with 480 P126-XFSAILD-SKIP-AGMETA lines after its P482-UMOUNT-AGREL (xfsaild refusing dirty AG-metadata items for AGs whose grant it had published), 460 P88-PUBOB-RECLAIM-REFUSED, 370 P141-UNLK-EXCLR; the 27 waiters log P-SB-SUMMARY-BAST (refused while held, D-0537 rule). The 4 nodes that reached the lock before test1 unmounted in ~1 s. No hung-task warnings, no shutdowns. Candidates (a) and (c) and sess487's (d) are NOT what the stacks show (no AG acquire, no inode DLM acquire, no iclus path in any umount or worker stack). GPT RULE: CONSULT ANOTHER MODEL WHEN STUCK ruling (sess487): occurrence reproduced; SB-lock amplification PROVEN; the chain 'post-publication inactivation -> dirty AG-meta AIL item for a published AG -> refused by xfsaild -> xfs_ail_push_all_sync never completes' is strongly supported but strict proof needs item/LSN correlation (the P126 line carries no item identity — filed as D-AIL-UNHELD-GRANT-SKIP-PERMANENT-SILENT-PIN-0487 next step 1). The lock scope itself is filed as D-SB-SUMMARY-LOCK-HELD-ACROSS-UNBOUNDED-LOG-QUIESCE-FLEET-CONVOY-0487. On 0.69.3 the same workload unmounted 28/28 measured nodes cleanly (4 unmeasured by a harness bug, no kernel hang on them). || SESS487 CANDIDATE (d), code-derived, UNMEASURED: on 0.69.2 mxfs_iclus_purge_all ran BEFORE the inactivation flush inside mxfs_sb_summary_final_sync (0.69.3 moved the purge after the flush, sess485 memory). purge_all (xfs_mxfs_dlm.c ~57697) removes and kfrees every inode-cluster lock object of the mount WITHOUT releasing their on-disk grants (those are swept by caw release_all inside v5_shutdown), so an inactivation that then takes a cluster lock (mxfs_iclus_lock ~57015) builds a NEW object at disk_mode NL over a slot that still carries this node's own EX bit: the claim self-EDEADLKs, fan_out has nothing to arm, and the SELFCLEAR escape refuses while any covered sibling is active — which with hundreds of siblings in the same clusters being inactivated concurrently is the normal state — so the caller retries into the documented '32 nodes starved 380s+' livelock shape (P-ICLUS-SELFCLEAR 'NOT cleared' ratelimited). Predicts: hung-node stacks in mxfs_iclus_lock / mxfs_v5_dlm_iclus_lock under the inodegc worker, P-ICLUS-SELFCLEAR lines in the unfiltered journal, and the fix leg clean because no cluster-lock consumer runs after the purge. Whether the inactivation's ILOCK even reaches mxfs_iclus_lock when the inode's cached i_dlm_mode is already EX is NOT established from the code; the lap-3 stacks decide. || UNKNOWN. Candidates, none measured: (a) the post-publication inactivation flush (inside mxfs_sb_summary_final_sync on 0.69.2) re-acquires the just-published AG through a fresh CAW acquire and something in that path never grants (own retained holder bit, latched state cleared by the release — the D-0528 / D-488 family); (b) a 32-way convoy on the SB summary EX lock, taken after publication on 0.69.2, whose BAST is refused while held so the peer waits on its own bounded CAW poll (D-0537 shape); (c) the bast-arm gate closes at put_super entry and an inactivation's inode DLM acquire wedges in a dead-demote re-drive the closed gate refuses (P-DEMWAIT-REDRIVE -> P6S-ARM-REFUSED every 3 s, the chain 116 v3 shape). The fix leg took the same SB lock 32 ways in 15 s and flushed inactivation after the same gate closure with no hang, which weakens (b) and (c) but does not exclude them: the timing and the queued state at closure differed. Bimodal timing (9 nodes at ~1 s, 23 nodes > 240 s, nothing between) argues for a wait that never completes rather than a slow path.

defects.summary: The directory LEAF hash index (a derived structure) can be left durably inconsistent with the directory's DATA blocks after a node death and foreign replay: readdir lists a name whose hashed lookup returns ENOENT, or the hash index reflects an unlink whose data block still carries the dirent. Since sess22 MXFS has masked the lookup face with mxfs_dir2_datascan_lookup (xfs/libxfs/xfs_dir2_leaf.c ~1842): on every ENOENT in a multi-node directory it linearly reads EVERY data block looking for the name, and the remove path has a twin (mxfs_dir2_leafless_removename) that expunges a dirent the leaf does not reference. On 2026-09-04 the heal fired for real (P22-DATASCAN-HIT) in two events: (1) 08:36:45-51, dir ino 75513091, names node17_f42.md5..node17_f45.md5 (the LAST four adds of one node) at data block 58 of 63, healed on test1/14/15/16 (76 lines; the five run directories 083456Z..085524Z that carry them share one boot journal), a hole in the direction DATA-AHEAD-OF-LEAF; (2) 10:49:14-21, dir ino 117440640, names pre_0001/0011/0021/0031/0041_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxx at block 0 of 3 on test2/test4 — this one is the D-0492 crash-durability CONTROL lap s493f on the deliberately buggy 0.70.9 build (RESULT FAIL unlinked-reappeared 5/5): block 0 reverted below the victim's fsync'd unlinks while the leaf kept their removal, LEAF-AHEAD-OF-DATA, and the heal resurrected dirents pointing at freed inodes (P26-IGET-FAIL err=-2). Event (2) is the closed D-0492 defect reproduced on purpose; event (1) is the live population on a current build. Either direction is the same class: after death+replay the directory's data and index blocks sit at different points in history. The root that leaves them torn was never ledgered: the heal made the lookup face disappear from every board row.

The lookup-cost link: tests/evidence/sess494_lkp_attrib_s495c.log LKP-TRACE windows=3203 bio_total=19200 (xfs_dir3_data 16331), per-window p50=1 p90=20 max=35; full log run_crash_consistency_20260904T124810Z kernlog_test17.gz P26-DSCAN 171 in 100 lookups, ndb 2..38. The workload's names have no xfs_da_hashname bucket larger than 2 (tools/xfs_dahash_collisions.py --cc 32 100), so the hashed lookup itself cannot account for the reads.
defects.mechanism: UNPROVEN, two candidates (RULE: CONSULT ANOTHER MODEL WHEN STUCK review sess496). (1) Durability cut at a kill: MXFS destages directory DATA blocks OUT-OF-LOG at grant release (direct write + flush) while the LEAF block's update travels through the CIL; if the node dies after the data flush but before the CIL record carrying the leaf update is forced (or before the leaf home write), the peer's foreign replay recovers the last committed leaf state, which predates the tail adds — data present, hash entries absent, durably. The 'last N adds of one node' shape and the persistence across replays fit this. (2) Stale foreign replay: a foreign log slice carries an OLDER image of the same leaf block and replay applies it over a newer home image without a globally ordered per-buffer veto (the D-FOREIGN-REPLAY-UNGATED-IMAGES family). The no-crash occurrence (pre_0041 in chain-139 rows) says at least one path forms holes in live operation: candidates are the release drain writing a stale leaf image, a leaf rebuild/compaction or block->leaf/leaf->node conversion omitting entries, or a late notification-driven invalidate replacing an in-core leaf with a stale platter image. Consequences today: (a) every ENOENT lookup in a shared directory whose coherency key moved pays an O(dir) cold data-block walk — measured p90 20, max 35 reads per create lookup, the 4.85 ms term that keeps the crash_consistency board row red; (b) the heal is name-specific, so any attempt to gate it (e.g. per-tenure) turns a hole for name B into a DUPLICATE dirent on create(B) or an ENOENT on unlink/rename of B; (c) a lookup path that does not route through the heal (any caller bypassing xfs_dir_lookup_args' ENOENT tail) sees the hole.
defects.found: sess496, while attributing the shared-directory create lookup term (D-32NODE-SHARED-DIR-CREATE-PACE) with the 0.70.15 lookup-window read trace. The trace showed the lookup linearly reading every data block of the directory; the reader is mxfs_dir2_datascan_lookup, the sess22 'leaf-hash hole heal', and a day-wide census showed the heal is still repairing real holes.
defects.next:
SESS577: ONE CANDIDATE DISPOSED BY REASONING, THE DECISIVE INSTRUMENT NOW EXISTS, AND 232 CLEAN WITNESSES AT 2/TCP INCLUDING ACROSS A NODE DEATH. RECORD STAYS OPEN.

CANDIDATE 1 (durability cut at a kill: DATA destaged out-of-log at release while the LEAF update is still in the CIL) IS DEAD, and not for lack of reproduction. A design consult established that under a log force that actually covers the transaction, a skipped LEAF home write is not a durability hole at all: recovery supplies the LEAF update, so the crash cut data=T / leaf=T-1 is harmless. The only premise that could have rescued the candidate was that the log force does not really persist, since the journal writes ride bio REQ_PREFLUSH/REQ_FUA (xfs_log.c 2889 and 2906) rather than the explicit SCSI WRITE(16)+FUA helper this project built because the target drops those bio flags. That premise was checked and does not apply: pal/linux/xfs_super.c 3264 declares a COHERENCE-ONLY durability domain in which target power loss is explicitly out of scope, and this defect is NODE death, which is in scope, where the journal lives in the target coherent cache and the survivor reads it. So the force is sufficient for the in-scope failure mode and candidate 1 cannot produce this tear.

A THIRD REPAIR WAS FOUND, AND IT SAT EXACTLY WHERE THE MEASUREMENT HAD TO BE TAKEN. This record names two masks, the datascan lookup heal and the leafless removename, and every prior experiment toggled those through dir_datascan_heal. mxfs_dir_rebuild_leaf_from_data is a third, on a SEPARATE knob (dir_leaf_rebuild, default 1), fired from xfs_dir_createname gated on a flag armed once per cross-node tenure and consumed BEFORE that tenure first mutation. The leaf it finds there is the one the node ACQUIRED from the handoff. It rebuilt that leaf from the data blocks and reported only the rebuilt count, so a directory that arrived torn was made whole in place and never reached a board row. That is why every instrument aimed at this defect, all of which look after recovery, found nothing: the repair was consuming the measurement at the one point an incoherent acquisition is visible.

WHAT LANDED, 0.79.0: the rebuild now snapshots the acquired hashval/address set before overwriting it and diffs it against the derived set in one merge pass over entries already in hand. missing means present in the data and absent from the acquired index, which is the readdir-lists-it / lookup-ENOENTs face. extra means the index references a dirent the data does not carry. Both outcomes are reported, P496-ACQ-DIVERGE and P496-ACQ-CLEAN, because an instrument that speaks only on failure cannot be distinguished from one that never ran. Report-only, no behaviour change, no extra I/O, and the repair is untouched. Detection is now separable from repair, which the earlier ruling on retiring the masks required and which nothing in the tree previously provided.

MEASURED, AND NON-VACUOUS. Lap s577a, tests/sess493_d0492_crash_durability.sh at 2 nodes over TCP, build 77B44618AD2DA40BC1A3C38, MODARGS dir_datascan_heal=0 with the harness own capture confirming heal=0 on every node, so a leaf hole would have failed the verify instead of being repaired at lookup. 12/12 rounds, victim test1 destroyed with the attempt standing, survivor fenced and replayed, RESULT PASS missing=0 extra=0, replay_complete=1, refused=0, quarantine=0, shutdown=0. On the survivor: 196 acquisition censuses on the lap shared directory and 33 on the earlier shared-dir reuse workload, 229 total, EVERY ONE CLEAN, zero divergence. The coverage check is exact, 229 censuses against 229 rebuilds, so the instrument fired on every repair rather than going silent. A separate earlier run of dir_reuse_coherency gave 36 more clean censuses against 36 rebuilds and PASSED 2/2 at 106s of a 120s budget, so the census costs nothing measurable.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH, STATED PLAINLY. It is a bounded negative, not a disposition. 38 further rebuilds declined on directory format, so the window covers single-leaf directories only and says nothing about node-format ones. The diff ran against this node in-core data blocks, not the platter image, because the platter-union arm is behind dir_leaf_rebuild=2 and that arm is known delete-unsafe, so it was deliberately not enabled. The lap is SINGLE-WITNESS by construction at two nodes. And the live population in this record, node17_f42..f45.md5 on dir 75513091, came from a 32-node workload that this shape does not cover. The victim own pre-crash census is unrecoverable in any case because its journal is volatile and it was power-cycled.

NEXT, IN ORDER. 1) Extend the census to node/BTREE-format directories, since the rebuild bails there and that is where the original 32-node evidence lived; the bail counter already tells you how much population is being skipped. 2) Get a durable-source comparison without enabling the delete-unsafe union: read the platter image for the diff only, never feeding it into the rebuilt leaf. 3) Repeat laps for a witness count rather than trusting one. 4) The remaining live candidate is stale foreign replay applying an older leaf image over a newer home image; the census now gives the before-and-after pair at the acquiring node that this hypothesis needs, so instrument the replay decision for leaf buffers and correlate its disposition against the next acquisition census on the same directory.

defects.summary: When both nodes of the cluster unmount at the same time, each node's clean departure sends its remaining grant releases to their master, which is the peer, and the peer has already begun its own teardown and drops LOCK_RELEASE messages (P-TEARDOWN-MSG-DROP: after ctx->mounted clears only NODE_LEAVE and RELEASE_ACK pass). The releaser resends three times and then waits the whole 3 s ack bound (P-TAUTH-RELEASE-WAIT unacked=N after 3000ms) before completing the unmount, so a whole-cluster shutdown costs every node 3 s plus the quiesce (4.5 to 8.9 s per unmount measured against a native XFS unmount of well under a second), and the peer-mastered ACTIVE records of the departed incarnation stay on the platter for the next mount to import as blockers and release as residue (P-TAUTH-IMPORT-RESIDUE) instead of being retired at departure. 0.75.17 fixed the single-departure shape (the ACK was being dropped); the concurrent shape drops the RELEASE itself.

Each node is the master of half the pages, so half of every node's releases are addressed to a peer that is itself past the quiesce. What is NOT yet measured: the cost the retained records impose on the next whole-cluster mount without a re-mkfs (import-residue count and its wall), and whether MODE=serial unmounts (the control) complete in the sub-second the quiesce alone needs.

The takeover's platter pass is now ~2.4 s for 206 MiB (about 86 MiB/s) and its 212 page prepares+activations another 2.4 s; both are recovery-time costs on the survivor after a DEATH, not unmount costs. STILL OPEN FOR MECHANISM (2): the concurrent-unmount LOCK_RELEASE drop at a tearing-down master (v5_mount.c ~1158 passes only NODE_LEAVE + RELEASE_ACK through the quiesce; the releaser resends every MXFS_DLM_RELEASE_RETRY_MS=1000 ms and mxfs_dlm_wait_release_acks bounds at 3 s). The idle parallel laps show no wait because an idle mount has no cross-mastered grant left; the post-workload parallel unload (chain s550, WORKLOAD=agmeta_stale_leak_2node) is the measurement for it. Design under consideration: pass LOCK_RELEASE through the quiesce once the departing node's own release_all walk has finished (no local entry can then be promoted; process_remote_release only commits the retirement on a page this node still masters and acks), until its GOODBYE; a page already PREPARED by handoff_depart refuses the commit and the ack says REMASTER, so the releaser re-routes as today. || SESS544 ATTRIBUTED from the P-DEPART-WORK lines (s545d test2, s545b test1, s544g test2): purge_ms=4568/3969/4412 and takeover scan_ms=4371/3975 over scanned=26426 pages (cand=0-5, pages_prepared=0) — each pass reads BOTH copies of every page (2 x 26426 x 4 KiB = 206 MiB) at the LUN's ~50 MiB/s, twice per departure = 8-9 s, for a handful of candidates. The unmount wall IS these two scans (plus the 3 s unacked wait in the concurrent shape). FIX SHAPE (measurements first): (a) the purge needs no platter scan — a page can only be ACTIVE(self) through this node's own cache (commit/activate require the cached page ACTIVE(self)), so walk the cached pages instead of the region; (b) the takeover's candidate selection needs only each copy's 128-byte header (auth_node/authority_epoch), so scan headers (26 MiB, ~0.5 s) and read full pages only for candidates; (c) both scans share one pass. Verify: P-DEPART-WORK purge_ms + takeover_ms under 500 ms on the 26426-page rig, unmount wall under 1 s serial, and the same records retired (cand and imported_dropped unchanged). || SESS544 serial CONTROL measured (tests/fleet_unload_check.sh MODE=serial s545d, 0.75.64 sv 90BA2F91, idle fresh mount, tests/evidence/20260908T214051Z_unload_s545d): first node out (test1, peer still up) umount 619 ms, no release wait; LAST node out (test2) umount 4776 ms with NO release wait either — its timeline: P-SB-SEALED at +0.08 s, P-TAUTH-PURGE-OWNER +0.38 s, P304-PR-WORKER +0.53 s, then nothing until P-TAUTH-TAKEOVER / P-DEPART-WORK / P-RELALL-* / P-GOODBYE-SENT / P-SB-SEAL-OK all at +4.75 s. In the parallel case (s545b test1, 8466 ms): PURGE-OWNER at +4.4 s, TAKEOVER/DEPART-WORK/GOODBYE-SENT at +8.4 s. So the unmount wall is dominated by the departure ledger passes (the peer's purge + takeover over the whole tauth region, ~4 s each, run on the departing node for the peer that left before it, serialized ahead of its own release_all/GOODBYE), plus the 3 s unacked-release wait only in the concurrent shape. Two mechanisms: (1) the sole-survivor/last-out node runs the departed peer's purge+takeover passes (~4 s of region reads) BEFORE its own departure work, and the first-out node in the parallel case does the same for its peer; (2) the dropped LOCK_RELEASE at a tearing-down master. Both are RULE: TIMEOUTS ARE PERFORMANCE ASSERTIONS, NOT SAFETY NETS unmount pace; native umount is sub-second.
