defects.summary: A demoter claim taken when a BAST is deferred to a transaction's end (mxfs_inode_dlm_defer_bast) outlived its release by 10 s: the inode stayed DEMOTING with mode EX and no holder, every peer BAST was swallowed as having no live demoter, and peers waited until the stale-requeue path ran the release in a kworker.
defects.evidence: tests/evidence/run_chk_clean_20260930T173640Z-g8/kernlog_test7.gz (rank 1) at 17:47:36: P126-DEMOTE-RACE ino=17309339 mode=5 state=3 ex=0 pr=0 bast_pending=0 work_busy=0 demoter_set=1 dem_pid=26614 dem_comm=rm dem_line=30:1206 (the claim set in mxfs_inode_dlm_defer_bast of that build) dem_age_ms=10225, then P72-SWALLOW-DEAD and P72-STALE-REQUEUE; kernlog_test11.gz P34-ACQ-SLOW ino=17309339 dur_ms=10230. No P152-TRANSDRAIN-PUNT on that inode in the 10 s before, so the claim was not retained by the documented punt: the transaction-end drain that should run the release and clear the claim (mxfs_trans_drain_inode_unlocks) did neither for this entry. Across five 8-node waves: one claim older than 1 s (this one); P126 fired 22-324 times per wave with every other claim younger than 1 s.
defects.next: Name the exit that leaves the claim: P-DEMOTER-NOGRANT (0.90.37) prints claim_age_ms and claim_line whenever a stale claim asks to bypass, and the per-inode claim ring (mxfs_demev_rec) records every set and clear. Candidates read in the code, not measured: a transaction cancelled after the defer (does xfs_trans_cancel reach mxfs_trans_drain_inode_unlocks?), and a pending entry moved to another transaction by xfs_trans_roll/dup. Instrument: count defers per transaction and drains per transaction, and print a transaction freed with a pending entry its drain did not process. ===== A CLAIM WHOSE TASK EXITED IS INHERITED BY A LATER PROCESS (measured with the test injector, lap tests/evidence/stress_rmrace_20261001T013810Z-g8-mkdir): a claim planted on the base directory by an rm that then exited (P-DEMOTER-KEEP-INJECT ino=131 pid=2141 comm=rm at 01:39:18) was presented 12.2 s later by a mkdir, pid 2190, whose task structure had been reused (P-DEMOTER-NOGRANT ino=131 claim_age_ms=12182 claim_line=21:5586 pid=2190 comm=mkdir). The claim is a bare task_struct pointer compared with current (mxfs_is_demoter), so after the owner exits any process that gets the same task structure is treated as the drain: it is admitted by the demoter bypass (refused since 0.90.37 when no drain is behind the claim), and it also skips every demote wait that exempts a demoter. A leaked claim therefore reaches unrelated processes, not only its own task. Candidate hardening to evaluate as its own change, after the leak's exit is named: a claim counts only while the stamped i_dlm_demoter_pid equals current->pid. ===== CHANGE (0.90.37, srcversion 5F51132AEEFCE6E024C15D7, then 85AEE4625B3EA2BBDBA2B96 which adds only the DEAD-REAP name to two event-ring print tables): a claim slot now holds a task reference on its owner (taken by the side that wins the NULL->task swap, dropped by the side that wins the task->NULL swap: owner clear, punt sweep, final release, retirement), so a claimed task_struct can never be reissued to another task; and a claim whose owner has reached exit_state is retired (P-DEMOTER-DEAD-REAP) when a task checks for a foreign drain or tries to claim the inode, under a hashed lock shared with the punt sweep. Switch: demoter_dead_claim_reap (1 default, 0 control). The raw claim in mxfs_clayer/pinned_resource.c now goes through the claim helpers. This addresses the harm of a leaked claim, not the exit that leaks it, which is still unnamed. ===== CONTROL LAP (build 5F51132A, demoter_bypass_grant_gate=1 demoter_dead_claim_reap=0, injector on rank 1 allowed on the base directory; tests/evidence/stress_rmrace_20261001T030435Z-g8-mkdir): rank 1 planted 113 claims, wedged (P-INODE-WEDGE) and withdrew, made 3 mkdirs against ~980 on every other rank, audit STALE. Reproduces the dead-claim wedge of fix arm 2 (01:51Z) on the new build with retirement off. ===== FIX LAPS (build 85AEE4625B3EA2BBDBA2B96, demoter_dead_claim_reap=1, gate 1, injector allowed on the base directory; stress_rmrace_20261001T031156Z and stress_rmrace_20261001T032106Z): 13 and 15 dead-owner claims retired (10 and 9 on the base directory) by release workers 10-36 ms after planting, no wedge or withdraw, every rank returned, audits CLEAN. A dead owner's claim no longer stalls or wedges anything. STILL OPEN: the exit that leaks a claim with a LIVE owner (wave 1's 10 s stall) is not named; a live owner's claim is untouched by retirement. Next as before: count defers and drains per transaction and print a transaction freed with a pending entry its drain did not process.
defects.impact_why: Measured once on 8/net/mesh/direct (wave 1, 0.90.37 build 380DA50320094248C0E34A4): peers' acquires of one directory waited 10.2 s (P34-ACQ-SLOW dur_ms=10230) and their BASTs were swallowed while a stale claim held the inode in DEMOTING; the stale-requeue path then released it. No data was lost through this alone once the demoter bypass stopped admitting a claim with no drain behind it (demoter_bypass_grant_gate, 0.90.37); without that gate it was the precondition of D-8TCP-RM-OF-A-CHILD. A bounded stall, not a hang or a crash.

defects.summary: Every full-ledger scan of the TCP authority ledger (node-death takeover, the mount's orphan sweep, collecting a dead node's EX holdings) reads both shadow copies of every page, and mkfs sizes the ledger at one record per 64 KiB of device, so recovery time scales with LUN size rather than with what the ledger holds.
defects.evidence: 2026-10-01, 1 TB LUN, 2/net/mesh/direct: P-TAUTH-TAKEOVER 14.5 s, P-TAUTH-ORPHAN-SWEEP 14.6 s then 14.7 s, ~300 MB/s, sweep reported live_pages=1 of 541,201. 20 GB LUN (10,571 pages): 0.28-0.29 s each. Sizing: tools/mkfs_mxfs.c tauth_npages_for_device; cap MXFS_TAUTH_NPAGES_MAX=2^20 (include/mxfs/mxfs_tauth.h:112). Design consult 2026-10-01 (ccmemory ruling-tauth-ledger-recovery-scan-cost-sparse-summary-first): ship a crash-ordered sharded occupancy summary first; population sizing only after an enforced per-node record bound and a bounded page-full answer exist. ===== 0.90.39 boards, 20 GiB pool LUNs: orphan sweeps 75,063 ms (8017 pages, 8/net/mesh/direct g8), 83,801 ms (6494), 149,390 ms (16000 pages, 67,651-page ledger); takeovers 8-37 s. Per-phase store timers (P-TAUTH-STORE-STATS) average 0 ms per phase because they are kept in whole ms; a page takeover is ~3 conditional commits (prepare, activate, purge) of ~8 sub-ms I/Os each, which accounts for ~9 ms/page. The timers need microsecond resolution before step 1 of the batching ruling can decompose it.
defects.next: Consult 2 (2026-10-01, ccmemory ruling-tauth-recovery-cost-is-flush-amplified-takeover-batch-it-first): the cost is per-page authority-transition flushes, not the scan. Step 1: instrument dlm_takeover_page to decompose its ~9 ms (PREPARE write, flush, ACTIVATE write, flush, read/validate, lock wait). Step 2: batch takeover/sweep transitions with two barriers per chunk (PREPARED images -> flush -> ACTIVE images -> flush -> serve), PREPARED carrying transition identity; crash-inject every point; measure batch sizes. Step 3 (structural): range authority (view table, docs/tcp-authority-ledger.md item 7). Population-sized npages only after a page-full design; empty-page release only if cold-empty is measured large.
defects.impact_why: 0.90.39 boards on 20 GiB pool LUNs, 2026-10-01: orphan sweeps of 75-149 s (8017-16000 pages, ~9.3 ms/page) and node-death takeovers of 8-37 s ran under net/mesh/direct death-replay rows at 2, 4 and 8 nodes; 3188 requests were served by on-demand page takeover and the rest waited on the takeover's progress (P960-AUTH-TRANSITION-WAIT), not their retry budget. The survivors' logs (tests/evidence/20261001T{171417Z,191900Z,142521Z,174440Z,174341Z}_tcpdr_ca_*) hold no filesystem shutdown, hung task, oops or exhausted request, and every correctness row passed. A bounded recovery wait that grows with ledger size: pace, not a hang, crash, shutdown or data loss.

defects.summary: Every MXFS mount takes about 5 s whatever the LUN size, mostly a fixed 2.5 s boot-scan observation window (MXFS_BOOTSTRAP_SCAN_EARLY_MS, dlm/bootstrap.h:623) plus peer discovery; native XFS mounts in milliseconds.
defects.evidence: 2026-10-01 measurements across LUN sizes (20 GB .. 1 TB): mount call returns in ~5 s on any size, 7.6 s at 1 TB.
defects.next: Trace one mount phase by phase (boot scan, discovery, slot claim, log mount) and find which waits are fixed sleeps that a heartbeat-sequence read or an event could replace. ===== Mount-path wait map (2026-10-01, code read): candidates on a normal mount are the bootstrap survivor scan's 2500 ms poll whenever any heartbeat record is occupied (dlm/bootstrap.c:1138, MXFS_BOOTSTRAP_SCAN_EARLY_MS; a live peer costs one poll ~2.5 s, the heartbeat interval is 2 s), the membership-settle gates' 250 ms polls up to 15 s (v5_mount.c:17699 TCP, :18384 CAW), and the DLM acquire settle gate's 100 ms polls until every peer's view hash matches (dlm.c:7621, window mxfs_memb_settle_ms=20000). Next: phase-timed trace of a 2-node and an 8-node mount to see which dominates; then replace fixed polls with heartbeat-sequence reads / event wakeups.
defects.impact_why: mount latency only; nothing corrupts or crashes

defects.summary: After every node of an 8-node set rebooted, the first node to join the cluster again (alma9-2, RHEL 9.8, 8/net/mesh/direct, packaged 0.90.39) did not finish mount within 60 s; the other seven mounted. Whether the mount was slow or hung is not known: its kernel log was lost.
defects.evidence: 2026-10-01, full_verify 0.90.39 packaged round rhel9 8/net/mesh/direct (tests/evidence/packaged_round/rhel9_0.90.39_net-mesh-direct_20261001T180755): all 8 alma9 nodes rebooted and answered in 22-29 s; postboot mount_all ran node by node with MOUNT_S=60 from 18:21:53 CDT; alma9-1 formed the cluster (mount_rc=0), alma9-2's postboot_mount log is EMPTY (the ssh was killed by the 60 s timeout before mount returned), alma9-3..8 then mounted (mount_rc=0); round stopped 18:23:28 'FAIL: postboot mount'. The harness saved no kernel log and alma9-2 rebooted again at 23:37 UTC with a non-persistent journal, so its kernel log is gone. Host conditions then: a training job on clyde, 19.9 GB in swap, 1.2 GB free, host load 28-31. ===== Not reproduced: the rhel9 set re-run passed that step, and tests/packaged_round.sh POSTBOOT_LAPS=10 on the quiet host (tests/evidence/postboot_laps_rhel9_0.90.39.out) mounted all 8 after a whole-set reboot 10 times: the bootstrap 0.2-1.3 s, every joiner 4.8-5.2 s, one 9.0 s (alma9-8 lap 4); 80 of 80 under 10 s. Debian13 postboot: joiners 4.8-5.3 s.
defects.next: Open: cause unknown. Hypothesis to test: host memory pressure starved the joiner (clyde 19.9 GB swapped, training job) — run POSTBOOT_LAPS on rhel9 8/net/mesh/direct under a measured host memory load and see whether joins stretch; the harness now keeps the kernel log of any mount over MOUNT_S, so a recurrence names where the join waited. ===== SECOND OCCURRENCE 2026-10-04, full_verify 0.90.47, debian13 2/net/mesh/direct, four platform sets rebooting at once, host load 12-15 (tests/evidence/packaged_round/debian13_0.90.47_net-mesh-direct_20261004T165231): debian13-1 formed the cluster in 954 ms; debian13-2 (slot 0, fresh claim) logged P-BARRIER-GHOST-EXTEND undeclared=1 window_ms=62000 bound_ms=122000 at +3 s, 'mount recovery barrier complete: cohort=0x0' at +6 s, and then nothing up to the capture at +60 s (postboot_mount_fail_kernlog_debian13-2.log, 603 lines). A passing mount prints 'peer_joined cb registered post-multi' and 'statfs perag baseline initialized' in the same second as the barrier line, from after xfs_mountfs returns, so the wait is inside xfs_mountfs after the barrier (the root inode's first cluster acquires, or later). The first node's log was not kept. NOT REPRODUCED on the quiet set: tests/postboot_hang_capture.sh debian13 0.90.47, 6 laps then 30 laps under rig board load (tests/evidence/postboot_hang_debian13_0.90.47.out): 36 of 36 joiner mounts 5.08-5.72 s, bootstrap 0.19-1.1 s; every passing joiner also prints GHOST-EXTEND undeclared=1, and the first node prints P-TAUTH-TAKEOVER-DECERTIFIED (pages_prepared=0 remaining=229, 'no longer holds the lowest live slot') one second after the join. Untested hypothesis: the joiner's first acquire waits on a lock-table page whose takeover the first node dropped when the joiner took the lowest slot, until the dead window of the previous incarnation's record (62 s) runs out. Next: tests/postboot_hang_capture.sh keeps both nodes' mount and D-state task stacks and mxfs kernel lines when a lap fails; run it with all four platform sets rebooting together, the condition of both occurrences.
defects.impact_why: Both occurrences ended by themselves with no crash, shutdown or fence. rhel9 8/net/mesh/direct 0.90.39: about 100 s after the mount began the next round unloaded the module cleanly on that node and passed every check. debian13 2/net/mesh/direct 0.90.47: the mount was still in the kernel 63-73 s after it began (the next round's unload on debian13-2, tried for 10 s from 16:59:21 CDT, printed UNLOAD_FAILED refcnt=2 mounts=0), and 4.9 min after it began the same node, not rebooted in between, mounted a fresh filesystem with mount_rc=0 (tcp_peer_freeze_death/20261004T170311_debian13_net-mesh-direct/mount_debian13-2.txt). A join that overran its 60 s budget twice; pace, not a hang.

Rerun the row on 0.90.49 until it recurs or the two fixes of this build are shown to cover it. ===== 0.90.50 (2436A85B09810AB6EF34C94): path_fenced_return run 10 times on 2/net/mesh/mpath g2 (tests/evidence/ag_phantom_laps_hang_g2.out), 10 PASS, 214-244 s, no hang; this is not a disposition. The stuck-node capture in the path rows is what will name it if it recurs. ===== 0.90.52 (969D04DEE5EC7BC4C48CF17): path_fenced_return PASS on 2/net/mesh/mpath g2 in chain s11g2r and laps s11g2a, s11g2b, s11g2c (4 runs), no load left without its PATHLOAD line. Not a disposition. ===== ===== 2026-10-18 (session 98) CHAIN pfr95 EXTRACTED (2/net/mesh/mpath g2e, test17 survivor + test18 fenced, build 022F8BF6763B609A9ECC7D1, 8 laps of path_fenced_return + chk_clean, tests/evidence/lapchain_pfr95.out, per-lap logs board_2-net-mesh-mpath_path_fenced_return_chk_clean_g2e_pfr95<a..h>.log): no lap reproduced this record's hang; a DIFFERENT failure appeared in 3 of 8 laps. Code read: mxfs_dialloc_validate_candidate (xfs/libxfs/xfs_ialloc.c:1874) returns -EBUSY from two arms, P946-VALIDATE-PUBPEND (this node's own free not yet on the platter) and P947-VALIDATE-NOMAGIC (home holds no inode magic), and mxfs_dialloc_two_phase (:3620-3670) re-picks on -EBUSY up to 64 restarts. NEXT: grep the three failing laps' test17 kmsg (kmsg_test17_fromnode.gz in each board dir) for P946-VALIDATE-PUBPEND, P947-VALIDATE-NOMAGIC, P946-DIALLOC-PUBPEND-STORM and P-DIALLOC-VALIDATE-EIO in the second before each P-DIALLOC err=-16, then file the survivor's EBUSY create as its own record (it recurs, 3 of 8, so it is not a 99/1 corner case), predicting with tools/release_status.py which rows it turns red. ===== ===== 2026-10-18 (session 99) THE SURVIVOR EBUSY CREATES DID NOT COME FROM EITHER VALIDATE ARM. Each stream carries 40 P951-VALIDATE-OFF-SOLE lines ('a SOLE SURVIVOR is picking an inode with the D-0351/D-0946 platter validation OFF'), the nearest at 569 / 1271 / 3092 lines before each cluster. So the error was returned on the single-node allocation path (single=1), with the platter validation off. NOT YET ATTRIBUTED: which return in that path gives -EBUSY. NEXT: read xfs_dialloc and its sole-survivor branch for every -EBUSY return reachable with single=1, instrument the one not named by a probe, then file the survivor EBUSY create as its own record. ===== ===== 2026-10-19 (session 104) THE SURVIVOR'S EBUSY CREATES ARE FILED AS THEIR OWN RECORD, D-SOLE-SURVIVOR-CREATES-FAIL-EBUSY-FROM-DIALLOC-AFTER-PEER-FENCE (high, 2/net/mesh/mpath, noblock by its measured effects): xfs_dialloc ends its sweep on any xfs_dialloc_try_ag error but -EAGAIN, and the -16 comes from a callee no probe names. This record's own failure (a rejoined node's private write hung 133 s, its kernel log lost) has not recurred in the 22 path_fenced_return laps since (10 on 0.90.50, 4 on 0.90.52, 8 in pfr95). Also find why test7 never registered test13's goodbye. ===== ===== 2026-10-17 (session 20) FIRST RUN OF THE RACE HARNESS: VACUOUS. tests/mpath/umount_pair_race.sh, build 5E4D32A64FC67B3543A120C, 4/net/mesh/mpath g4, queue tests/queues/upr_relall_ab.queue (log tests/evidence/lapq_uprab.log): 4 laps alternating dl_relall_skip_unreachable=0/1, all PASS, but none reached the incident: B's release-all held 4-5 grants and sent nothing that failed (uprc1: 'P-RELALL-WALL released=4 ms=88 send_failed=0 skipped=0 step_ms=20 skip_unreachable=0', FAILED_SENDS=0; B umount 1288-1600 ms in both arms). The row's 30 s pathload leaves almost nothing held at the unmount (eviction releases inode grants before release-all), and nothing stops B from registering A's GOODBYE. The incident needs both: B holding hundreds of grants mastered by A at release-all (test7 P-RELALL-LEFT held=938) and A gone without B having processed its goodbye. Next: hold grants B will still own at release-all (cached PR on many A-mastered inodes that eviction retains, or measure what test7's 938 were), and delay B's GOODBYE processing (dbg_goodbye_rx_delay_ms, in the build) so its sends meet a closed peer; the control must then show send_failed > 0 before the arms mean anything. ===== 2026-10-18 (session 57) WHERE THE INCIDENT'S 938 GRANTS COME FROM (code read, not yet measured): xfs/xfs_mxfs_evict.c retains a clean, wire-confirmed PR grant across evict (mxfs_evict_retain_pr, P6R-RETAIN 'clean PR grant retained across evict (demand-released via noino BAST)') whenever the filesystem is not unmounting; such a grant has no in-core inode, so the unmount's evict_inodes never releases it and only dlm_wire_release_all does. So B holds hundreds of peer-mastered grants at its release-all after it stat'ed many files and its caches were dropped (the path rows' drop_caches). REPRODUCER DESIGN for tests/mpath/umount_pair_race.sh (not yet written): PF_HOLD_FILES=N (after the load: A creates N empty files in a fresh directory and syncs; B stats every one, taking PR, then drops its caches; count B's P6R-RETAIN since the mark; on 2 nodes about half are A-mastered) and PF_GOODBYE_DELAY_MS on B (dbg_goodbye_rx_delay_ms, dlm/v5_mount.c ~2901: a one-shot sleep on the receive thread before the GOODBYE is processed, after v5_hrx_drain/v5_rrq_drain). CAVEAT to settle in the code before choosing the delay: the sleep is on B's receive thread, so if B's DLM teardown joins that thread its unmount wall includes the delay in BOTH arms; then the arms must be graded on P-RELALL-WALL ms= and FAILED_SENDS (control > 0 with a release-all wall of about rel x step + A-mastered-after-departure x 3 x 100 ms; fix one failed master, P-RELALL-MASTER-UNREACHABLE, wall about rel x step), not on the unmount wall. ===== ===== 2026-10-18 (session 62) THE FORCED A/B (tests/queues/upr_relall_hold_ab.queue, label uph, main tree build 311877C431E1BB444562804, 4/net/mesh/mpath g4, log tests/evidence/lapq_uph.log) IS VACUOUS BY ITS RULES: uphc1 (skip_unreachable=0) released=1004 relall_ms=25641 goodbye_delay_fired=1 but send_failed=1 (reach needs >= 20); uphc2 and uphf2 goodbye_delay_fired=0 (unreached); uphf1 (skip=1) released=1004 relall_ms=24605 send_failed=1 skipped=14 PASS. Two unreached control laps make the A/B VACUOUS. WHY THE CONTROL CANNOT REACH THE INCIDENT ON THIS BUILD, from uphc1's kept log (tests/evidence/board_uphc1_umount_pair_race/relall_test6.txt) and the code: B (test6) logged P-DBG-GOODBYE-RX-DELAY at 576.18, then P-RELALL-MASTER-UNREACHABLE master=4022937081 rc=-107 at 578.50 even with the knob at 0 (the mark is taken in both arms, dlm/dlm.c:11412-11423; the knob only gates the skip at :11383-11388), FAILED_SENDS=2 (one release's three attempts), and no further failed send in 1004 releases. The first release to the departed A met a hard socket error, and mxfs_peer_send then shuts the socket down, sets the peer DISCONNECTED and fires disconnect_cb (dlm/peer.c:1141-1153); after that no release to A reached the send loop. The incident is different: test7 logged 928 'lock release to node ... failed, retrying' (each release's sends failing with the peer not ACTIVE, dlm/peer.c:1085-1087, -ENOTCONN at once) and NO goodbye or disconnect for test13, i.e. its peer entry for test13 was already non-ACTIVE through a path that delivered no disconnect to the DLM, while the release-all kept treating test13 as a live master. NEXT: from the incident's kept logs (tests/evidence/run_chk_clean_20261005T220000Z-g8/kernlog_test7.gz, kernlog_test13.gz; a log sweep is running) establish how test7's peer entry for test13 went non-ACTIVE with no disconnect callback (dlm/peer.c sets MXFS_CONN_DISCONNECTED at :507, :609, :746, :800, :891, :919, :952, :963, :982 besides the two paths that fire disconnect_cb), then a hypothesis and a reproducer that puts B's peer entry for A into that state before B's release-all. ===== 2026-10-18 (session 87) THE INCIDENT'S STATE, READ FROM ITS KEPT LOGS (log sweep of tests/evidence/run_chk_clean_20261005T220000Z-g8, dmesg -T wall clock): the record's 'test7 logged no goodbye or disconnect from it' is half wrong. test7 (3669228136) processed P-GOODBYE-RX for the six other nodes at 22:27:22-23 (kernlog_test7.gz:125086-126185) but never one for test13 (1552207459), which logged P-GOODBYE-SENT at 22:27:29 (kernlog_test13.gz:137975); test7's own DLM teardown had begun by 22:27:23 ('P-TEARDOWN-MSG-DROP type=17 from node 1552207459 -- DLM session is tearing down', 997 lines kernlog_test7.gz:127345..130072). test7 DID get the disconnect: 22:27:31 'communication with node 1552207459 lost (err -32)', 'TCP peer 1552207459 disconnected', P164-DEAD-NOTE, and 'P-TCPDEATH-DEFERRED node=1552207459 slot=2 nlive=1 -- fenced as the sole other member; grants and mastership stay FROZEN until its journal slice is replayed' (kernlog_test7.gz:133412-133417). Its release-all began at 22:27:32 (P-RELALL-LEFT held=938 pr=7 ex=931, :133421) and sent to that FROZEN, still-in-view master: 928 'lock release to node 1552207459 failed, retrying' 22:27:32..22:29:10 (464 x 2 attempts remaining, 464 x 1), then P-TAUTH-RELEASE-WAIT unacked=466. NEXT: read test13's side in the kept logs (tests/evidence/run_chk_clean_20261005T220000Z-g8/kernlog_test13.gz, 22:27:2x): its connection state toward test7 (3669228136) when the GOODBYE broadcast ran, and any send failure or skip to test7 in that broadcast (dlm/v5_mount.c ~22465 P-GOODBYE-SENT and the send loop before it); the 2-node reproducer then has to put B's receive of A's GOODBYE in that lost state, not merely delay it.

defects.summary: on the physical DRBD pair, creating a VM whose disk is on /mnt/shared (qm create --scsi0 shared:1: a 1 GiB sparse raw file in a new images/<vmid> directory, made under Proxmox's cluster-wide storage lock, which aborts the command after 60 s) took over 60 s on pve2 while both hosts ran a VM-like load (fio O_DIRECT 4 KiB randrw 60/40 QD16 on a 1 GiB file each), and the create failed; idle, the same allocation takes 0.54 s, and single creates in that directory take 35-816 ms
defects.evidence: MEASURED 2026-10-06 16:30:02-16:31:27 CDT on pve2 (0.90.78 tools, module 50181F68ACDCBCCD0671169), tests/pve_pair_failover.sh withdraw-guests (first fix-arm attempt, evidence tests/evidence/pve_pair_failover/20261006T212934Z-192.168.1.80): pve2 journal 'qm[28200]: starting task ...qmcreate:103' 16:30:02.09, 'VM 103 creating disks failed' / 'unable to create VM 103 - storage-shared-locked command timed out - aborting' 16:31:27.68; /etc/pve/priv/lock empty afterwards, cluster Quorate. Same step on 0.90.77 at 16:16 (control arm, same loads running): three VMs created and started in ~20 s each. Idle at 16:33 on pve2: pvesm alloc shared 990 vm-990-disk-2.raw 1G 0.54 s; qemu-img create 1G 0.15 s; touch in images/990: 0.095, 0.035, 0.816 s, and 0.45 s in the first try.
defects.next: Instrument before changing: under the same two loads, time each step of a disk allocation on pve2 (mkdir images/<id>, create, ftruncate, the config write) and sample the stuck task's kernel stack every 0.5 s (tests/pve_pair_concurrency.sh has the sampler); compare with the same loads on local storage. Decide from the stacks whether the wait is a lock handoff to pve1, a log force behind the guests' writes in the DRBD/disk queue, or the write cap. ===== 0.90.104 (EFA0126F0369FF0A4246E54) physical pair 2026-10-08 03:40-04:02 CDT, tests/pve_alloc_under_load.sh (pvesm alloc 1G under fio 4k randrw QD16 per participant): two-host shape (loads on pve1+pve2, allocs on pve2) worst 13.2 s / 8.6 s, 0 failed, idle 1.0-5.1 s -- no allocation near Proxmox's 60 s lock any more. A/B on ONE host (both loads and the allocs on pve1, interleaved, tests/evidence/alloc-ab-0.90.104-*.log): MXFS worst 9.2 / 8.8 s, idle 1.5-3.6 s; XFS on a scratch DRBD resource (thick, same disks, scripts/pve_drbd_xfs_storage.sh) worst 5.1 / 1.5 s, idle 1.0 s. pvesm itself costs ~1.0 s idle. MXFS > 2x the XFS-on-DRBD yardstick under load: still a pace defect. The waits (stack samples, tests/evidence/pve_alloc_under_load/20261008T084025Z) are cluster lock requests pending (dlm_lock_impl pending_wait, mxfs_ilock_wait_for_transition in xfs_create/xfs_dir_lookup) while both disks are saturated: each grant is a ledger commit whose replicated writes queue behind the guests' I/O. Next: split one slow alloc's wall into its lock requests (which resources, master, commit time) with tests/pve_pair_profile.sh during the load.
defects.impact_why: a Proxmox VM create fails ('storage-shared'-locked command timed out) while other guests on the pair do I/O; no data is lost and no node is affected, but the operation the storage exists for fails

defects.summary: on the physical DRBD pair (HP Z400 x2, Kingston SSDNow V+ SATA SSDs at queue depth 1 with a volatile write cache, gigabit), AlmaLinux 9.7 installs with their disks on /mnt/shared take about twice as long as on local-lvm, and six at once (two on pve1, four on pve2) all missed packer's 45 min SSH timeout without finishing the install
defects.evidence: 0.90.78 (50181F68ACDCBCCD0671169), scripts/pve_pair_builds.sh: one build per host on shared (tests/evidence/pve_pair_builds/20261006T234148Z) installed after 1493 s (pve1) and 1346 s (pve2), guests' virtio writes 3.5 GiB in 29.5k ops averaging 345-350 ms, 12k flushes averaging 30-33 ms, each host's sda 40-43% busy; one build per host on local-lvm (20261006T224053Z) installed by ~720 s. Six at once on shared: pve1's two (20261007T003839Z) never answered as installed in 2784/2744 s (writes averaging 474-531 ms, flushes 62-65 ms; pve1 swapped until 19:50 with four), pve2's four (20261007T005727Z, started 19:58) never answered in 2731-2742 s though each wrote 3.31-3.39 GiB (a whole install's worth), writes averaging 889-973 ms, flushes 90-114 ms; pve2's sda 43% busy, 6.5 MiB/s, 32 flushes/s at 15.9 ms. Earlier (CHANGELOG 0.90.81): one 256 KiB QD8 direct writer: local ext4 147 MiB/s, raw scratch DRBD 11.0, XFS on DRBD 11.8, MXFS 13-16. Raw DRBD with four QD16 1 MiB writers per host: 48-52 MB/s.
defects.next: Attribute before changing anything: the same VM-like writes (scripts/drbd_write_latency_probe.sh vmio-mxfs, vmio-xfs, vmio-local: O_DIRECT 4-256 KiB random writes at QD4 with an fdatasync every 3, into a sparse file) on MXFS, on XFS over a scratch DRBD resource (thick and thin backing) and on a local XFS, on the idle pair; then one install on XFS over DRBD beside one on MXFS. What MXFS adds over XFS on the same DRBD is the defect to fix; what DRBD costs on these disks (a synchronous drain and cache flush on the receiver at every epoch, wo:f) is the hardware's, to be measured with the disks' write cache off too (hdparm -W0: no volatile cache, so DRBD's flushes cost nothing and stay safe) and stated in docs/drbd-setup.md as the pair's capacity. ===== ATTRIBUTION 2026-10-06 20:59-21:08 CDT, idle pair on 0.90.81, scripts/drbd_write_latency_probe.sh vmio-mxfs vmio-xfs vmio-local (one writer on pve2, 60 s each: O_DIRECT random writes 4/64/128/256 KiB 35/25/20/20 at QD4, fdatasync every 3, into a sparse 3 GiB file; scratch DRBD and local LVs thick). Write cache on (tests/evidence/drbd_vmio/20261007T015944Z-wc-on): MXFS on DRBD 5.6 MiB/s, write mean 35.8 ms, sync mean 72.2 / p99 675 ms; XFS on scratch DRBD 6.1 MiB/s, 41.7 ms, sync 39.4 / p99 380 ms; XFS on a local LV 10.7 MiB/s, 23.1 ms, sync 22.7 / p99 240 ms; the peer pve1's disk 60-70% busy in the DRBD arms, pve2's 30-47%, pve2's 88% in the local one. Write cache off on both disks (20261007T020424Z-wc-off, hdparm -W0, restored after): flushes fell to 0.3-0.5/s and every write slowed instead (w_await 7-17 -> 15-20 ms): MXFS 5.6 MiB/s sync 61.6 ms, XFS on DRBD 5.4 MiB/s sync 43.1 ms, local 9.8 MiB/s. So: DRBD protocol C on these disks costs ~1.8x local for this pattern whatever the write cache (every write waits for both disks, the peer's the busier), and the installs' 1.9-2.1x matches it; MXFS adds ~0-9% throughput and 1.4-1.8x sync latency over XFS on the same DRBD. Next: profile MXFS's fsync on vmio-mxfs against vmio-xfs (log force, coordination writes, the write bound) for its own share of the sync latency; then state in docs/drbd-setup.md the pair's write capacity (both disks write everything, so the pair has one disk's random-write capacity) and size the owner's builds to it. ===== MXFS's OWN SHARE, 21:08-21:25 CDT (tests/evidence/drbd_vmio/*): thin vs thick backing is not it (XFS on a pre-written thin scratch DRBD 6.3 MiB/s, sync 37.8 ms; thick 6.1, 39.4). MXFS on DRBD matches XFS on DRBD in throughput (6.6-7.0 MiB/s over 5 runs) but its fsyncs stay slower (60-72 ms vs 38-43 ms) while its writes complete faster (25-36 vs 41-49 ms). A 95 s ftrace profile on pve2 (tests/evidence/pve_pair_profile/vmio-mxfs-*) puts MXFS's own write-path code near zero (mxfs_ilock_fallible 0.02 ms, mxfs_ioq_admit_one 0.00 ms) and fsync's time in the XFS log force (xfs_log_force_seq 58.6 ms mean, xlog_wait_on_iclog 33.7 ms, xlog_cil_force_seq 1.9 ms); the only MXFS extra was the heartbeat's emulated swaps (mxfs_pal_drbd_cas_emulate 0.54/s at 105 ms). HYPOTHESIS that the heartbeat's swap writes on the same DRBD stream cost the sync latency: DISPROVED by an alternating A/B with both hosts' heartbeats paused 45 s (dl_inject_hb_pause_ms, inside the 60 s lease): control 7.0/7.0 MiB/s sync 64.5/66.4 ms, paused 7.0/6.7 MiB/s sync 66.0/67.3 ms (a single earlier 25 s pair, 6.9 vs 9.7 MiB/s, was noise). Next: the ~25 ms of xfs_log_force_seq outside xlog_wait_on_iclog (xlog_force_lsn's wait on the previous iclog's write, ic_prev SYNCING) on MXFS against the same function on the scratch XFS (profile xfs.ko's functions too), then a real install on XFS over DRBD beside one on MXFS. ===== 0.90.97 (9AAB71AAAFAB20F6F2390CF) physical pair 2026-10-07 14:36-15:21 CDT: 7 builds on shared (3 on pve1, 4 on pve2, sized to memory), 0 of 7 answered as installed within 2604 s (local-lvm baseline, same 7: installed in 1112-1256 s, 20261007T162925Z); guests' virtio writes 0.97-1.35 s mean (pve2 VMs 843-1352 ms per write), flushes 120-184 ms; host sda 68% (pve1) / 42% (pve2) busy, 7.2-7.4 MiB/s written, 38-41 flushes/s. Same outcome as 0.90.95 (20261007T165057Z). The log write is stock XFS (one bio with REQ_PREFLUSH|REQ_FUA; fua_disable does not touch it), so MXFS's extra fsync time is not the log write's flags; next: what else forces MXFS's log during a guest fsync (count xfs_log_force callers on vmio-mxfs vs vmio-xfs). ===== A/B ON THE SAME REPLICATION, physical pair 2026-10-07 (0.90.97 on the hosts): 3 Alma 9.7 builds on pve1 only (scripts/pve_pair_builds.sh COUNTS='3 0' STOP_INSTALLED=1 BUILD_BUDGET=2604), pve2 idle. XFS on a scratch DRBD resource, both hosts Primary, thick LVs (scripts/pve_drbd_xfs_storage.sh, STORAGE=drbdxfs; evidence tests/evidence/pve_pair_builds/20261007T204316Z): installed after 1596/1608/1619 s, guest writes 296-332 ms mean, flushes 29-32 ms, pve1 sda 6.5 MiB/s 84 writes/s 35.9 ms 34% busy. MXFS (STORAGE=shared; 20261007T211110Z): 2097/2182/2191 s, writes 474-517 ms, flushes 47-50 ms, pve1 sda 5.1 MiB/s 101 writes/s 49.2 ms 42% busy. MXFS = 1.33-1.37x XFS on the same DRBD (inside the 2x ceiling), and the 7-at-once failure is mostly the pair's capacity (XFS over DRBD needs ~1600 s for 3). Same bytes, but MXFS put 1.6x the write OPERATIONS on pve1's disk over its run (222k vs 136k); pve1's MXFS LV is thin with zeroing (64 KiB chunks, 65% provisioned) while the scratch LVs were thick, so first-write chunk zeroing is a candidate share. Next: count pve1 disk writes by origin under the MXFS builds (thin-pool provisioning vs coordination vs data), then decide. ===== 0.90.104 (4AFCD34789622F69480B4EE) physical pair 2026-10-08 04:57-05:20 CDT, scripts/pve_pair_builds.sh COUNTS='1 1' (tests/evidence/pve_pair_builds/20261008T095718Z): installed after 1368 s (pve1) and 1014 s (pve2), PASS within 2604 s; 0.90.78 took 1493 / 1346 s for the same; local-lvm ~720 s. Only kernel line: one P67-AG-BAST-STALL on pve1, no P113-DRAIN-WEDGE. The thin backing LV on pve1 is 84% provisioned with zeroing on (64 KiB chunks; pve2's is 100%): first writes into unprovisioned chunks on pve1 cost a chunk zeroing each -- a candidate share of the 1.6x write ops MXFS put on pve1's disk against XFS on a thick scratch LV; the A/B compared unlike backings. Next: an equal-backing A/B (fully provisioned or thick on both) and the guide to provision the backing volume up front. ===== 0.90.106 (3A36649EDAFA3E59C98E812), physical pair, scripts/pve_pair_builds.sh COUNTS='3 4' STOP_INSTALLED=1 BUILD_BUDGET=2604 TRACE=1, 08:27-09:12 CDT 2026-10-08 (tests/evidence/pve_pair_builds/20261008T132716Z, tests/evidence/builds-phys-0.90.106-3x4.log): 0 of 7 builds answered as installed within the 2604 s budget (every build rc=124); no I/O error in any guest's host log. ===== 0.90.106 crash-fix build (36AE6F621EFE1608895C6C3), physical pair, scripts/pve_pair_builds.sh COUNTS='3 4' STOP_INSTALLED=1 BUILD_BUDGET=2604 TRACE=1, 09:40-10:25 CDT 2026-10-08 (tests/evidence/pve_pair_builds/20261008T143942Z, tests/evidence/builds-phys-0.90.106-fix-3x4.log): 0 of 7 builds answered as installed within 2604 s (every build rc=124); kernel logs pve1 111 lines / pve2 92, I/O error=0, blocked for more than=0, WARNING=0, Shutting down filesystem=0, P-WITHDRAW=0 on both hosts. ===== 0.90.107 (36AE6F621EFE1608895C6C3) EQUAL-BACKING A/B, physical pair 2026-10-08, three AlmaLinux 9.7 builds at once on pve1 (pve2 mounted idle), scripts/pve_pair_builds.sh COUNTS='3 0' STOP_INSTALLED=1, MXFS's thin LV fully provisioned (99-100%) vs XFS on a thick scratch DRBD LV (scripts/pve_drbd_xfs_storage.sh): XFS-on-DRBD installed after 1630 / 1620 / 1609 s (tests/evidence/pve_pair_builds/20261008T204927Z), MXFS 2114 / 2105 / 2019 s with TRACE=1 (20261008T211715Z): worst 1.30x the yardstick, inside the 2x ceiling; no heartbeat stall, warning, hung task, I/O error or withdraw on either host. One build per host on MXFS (COUNTS='1 1', 20261008T202333Z): 1300 / 1013 s against local-lvm ~720 s. What remains unmeasured against a yardstick: both hosts loaded at once (XFS cannot be shared, so the per-host yardstick above is the comparison) at 3+4 builds.
defects.impact_why: measured as time only: every build that failed ended at packer's own SSH timeout (rc=1) with no I/O error in any guest, no withdrawal, refusal or RECOVERY_BLOCKED line on either host since 19:53 (one P278-HB-STALL each), both hosts mounted Primary/Primary UpToDate throughout

defects.summary: on the physical DRBD pair (0.90.81) a new file costs ~150-230 ms to create (p50, one host alone, p90 ~1 s), and a stat of a file the OTHER host just created costs ~170 ms with both hosts walking: du over 795 entries took 15.5 s on one host and did not finish in 190 s on both at once; once both hosts have read the tree the same walk takes 0.5 s
defects.evidence: 2026-10-06 21:29-21:47 CDT, pve1/pve2 0.90.81 (36AE66BA919CE8EC9AC9894), tests/pve_tree_walk.sh. (1) du -sh /mnt/shared (795 entries, files the failover tests' loads had written on both hosts): both hosts at once, killed at 190 s unfinished; then pve1 alone 15.5 s. (2) Warm (evidence 20261007T023543Z-192.168.1.80): p0, p0, p1 and both-at-once walks of the same 795 entries 509-515 ms each. (3) Cold (20261007T024425Z-192.168.1.80): seed0 (pve1 alone creates 50 x 4 KiB files, each fsynced): create p50 234 ms p90 926 ms max 1.48 s, total 18.6 s of 23 s; seed1 (pve2 alone): create p50 145 ms p90 1.06 s max 2.81 s; fsync p50 11-12 ms. Then both hosts walking /mnt/shared at once: 359 and 350 entries in 60 s (killed), progress per 5 s 2-62 entries, never stopped for longer than ~15 s. Sampled stacks: creates wait in mxfs_v5_dlm_inode_reserve_try -> mxfs_dlm_lock -> dlm_lock_impl pending_wait, msleep inside mxfs_dlm_lock_retries, and mxfs_tauth_ledger_commit page write/flush/read; the walkers in mxfs_v5_dlm_inode_lock pending_wait and the ledger commit (mxfs_tauth_page_write -> mxfs_pal_bdev_compare_and_write -> mxfs_pal_drbd_cas_emulate -> register writes waiting on both disks). The same cost as D-TCP-LEDGER-SMALLFILE-WORKLOAD-PACE-RULE0-0349 (a durable ledger page per grant), multiplied by DRBD: each ledger page commit is several synchronous writes that wait for both hosts' SATA disks, and the compare-and-swap is a bakery lock over DRBD.
defects.next: Profile one cold create and one cold peer-file stat on the pair with tests/pve_pair_profile.sh (mxfs_tauth_ledger_commit, mxfs_pal_drbd_cas_emulate, dlm_lock_impl, mxfs_dlm_lock_retries) to split the per-op time into ledger commits, CAS emulation and lock round trips; then design against the measured split (a PR grant that no replay needs should not cost a durable commit; batch ledger commits) ===== ===== RE-SEND VOLUME (physical pair 0.90.95, tests/evidence/pve_release_ack_trace/20261007T154703Z-192.168.1.80, seed + both-host walk + touch): pve2 received 1282 release acks that matched a pending release and 1250 that matched none (a duplicate's ack after the first retired it, or a not-yet answer), pve1 410 / 8; nested 1211/585 and 878/408. About half of pve2's releases were re-sent at least once, i.e. its master's release commit took over a second; the same per-commit cost as this record's creates and stats. ===== FLUSHES REMOVED, physical pair 2026-10-08 (tests/pve_ledger_commit_profile.sh: pve1 creates 100 x 4 KiB files each fsynced, peer idle, ftrace profile on both hosts). A ledger page commit on DRBD issued three empty flushes after writes that were already FUA; on DRBD an empty flush is a local flush plus a P_BARRIER the peer drains and flushes at. Baseline FFC718B71C6154E025033BC (clean runs 20261008T045113Z, base3, base4): 100 creates total 7.5/6.3/5.2 s, p50 32-34 ms, p90 49-212 ms, max 0.8-1.05 s; pve1 42 commits at 36-77 ms, pve2 61-63 at 54-69 ms; 3 flushes per commit at 1.9-2.7 ms; swaps 13-38 ms. 0.90.103 E51E9BB7579D782BE30A226 (store fua_durable on DRBD: no flush after a FUA write or swap; batched bodies FUA), clean runs phys-fua5/6: total 2.6/2.5 s, p50 23.8/24.4 ms, p90 34.1/31.7 ms, max 42/41 ms; commits 20-27 ms; swaps 11-17 ms; 0 flushes. (Runs fua1-4 carried the post-remount ledger takeover's 600-1200 page writes and are not comparable.) Still open: the peer-file stat cost (both hosts walking), a native-XFS-on-DRBD create yardstick for the 2x bar, and the two swaps per commit (a DRBD page could commit under ONE emulator lock acquisition: compare sector 0, FUA the whole page). ===== WALK ON 0.90.103 (E51E9BB7579D782BE30A226, flushes removed), physical pair 2026-10-08 00:39-00:42 CDT, tests/pve_tree_walk.sh seed both (evidence tests/evidence/pve_tree_walk/20261008T053915Z-192.168.1.80): seed, both hosts at once 400 files each fsynced: create p50 25-26 ms, p90 61-67 ms, max 0.3-0.57 s. Both hosts walking /mnt/shared at once: killed at 120 s with 2544 / 2604 entries done (~21 per s; budget 5 s): FAIL. Walker stack samples (233/235): 106/113 waiting on a remote inode lock (mxfs_dlm_lock_retries cond wait: the peer master's ledger commit), ~100 in this host's own ledger commits as master (emulated swaps, register writes, the body FUA write, the page reads), 12/7 reloading inodes from disk. A stat of a file the peer holds is a PR grant and the peer's release, each a durable ledger page commit. Next: one swap per single-page commit on DRBD (span commit) and remeasure; the remaining step is the design question whether a shared grant needs a durable record at all. ===== 0.90.103 SPAN COMMIT + SWEEP OFF ON TCP (D704B7503855CAE6A0F4F46, physical pair 2026-10-08 02:07-02:10 CDT): one-host creates (100 fsynced) 1.2-1.5 s total, p50 12 ms, p90 16-18 ms, commits 8.5-12 ms (phys-span1-3). Both hosts seeding 400 each: create p50 14.6 ms, p90 32 ms. Cold walk, both hosts at once over 3456 entries: 62.4 / 70.5 s (FAIL, budget 5 s), 4654/4776 ledger page commits per host at 15-17 ms: exactly one durable grant commit per host per entry. Warm repeat walk: 2646 entries in 1.0 / 0.5 s, 7 commits (PASS) -- before this build every walk was cold because dir_ex_bast_sweep dropped every idle read grant (interleaved A/B, tests/evidence/pve_knob_ab/20261008T063116Z). What remains is the cold read: a read grant is a durable ledger page commit before the stat can return (~19 ms an entry with both hosts walking). Removing it means a read grant whose record is not on the critical path (the takeover import installs holders only from platter records, so a new master's own unrecorded reads would have to be re-asserted), a design change across every takeover path. ===== 0.90.107 (36AE6F621EFE1608895C6C3, released), physical pair 2026-10-08 17:53-17:58 CDT, tests/pve_tree_walk.sh seed both p0 (tests/evidence/pve_tree_walk/20261008T225352Z-192.168.1.80): seed 400 fsynced 4 KiB files per host at once in 55.1 / 42.4 s (create p50 78.8 / 49.4 ms, p90 268 / 179 ms; fsync p50 11-14 ms). Both hosts walking /mnt/shared (3464 entries) at once: pve1 2432 entries when killed at 120 s, pve2 done in 110.9 s (FAIL, budget 5 s); pve1 alone afterwards 21.1 s (2685 entries in the first 5 s from cache, then ~50/s). WORSE than 0.90.103's 62.4 / 70.5 s for the same shape. The XFS yardstick is twice the 0.90.105 reading (30 MB/s) on an idle pair, so the gap is wider than recorded. Next: measure what the adaptive window settles at during the MXFS write (in-flight KiB and per-write completion latency) against the 500 ms target, and whether XFS's 63 MB/s itself holds the heartbeat swap within its margin. ===== 0.90.108 instrument (3DC4F1267FD87D78493DBDC, P-DRBD-IOQ-LAT completion-time histogram by class and depth at admission), physical pair pve1, lone dd 3 GiB conv=fsync 20.8 MB/s (tests/evidence/lone-writer-lat-0.90.108.log): data writes <100/<250/<500/<1000/<2000 ms admitted at <=4 MiB 73/188/76/5/1, <=8 MiB 70/706/1285/183/0, <=16 MiB 2/93/239/151/0; meta 29 writes, none over 500 ms; 99 cuts, win 7.9 MiB, peak 12.5 MiB, lat_max 1180 ms. Latency rises with depth (queueing), with a ~250 ms per-write floor (replication round trip + peer epoch drain), so rate ~ depth/(0.25 s + depth/70 MB/s): XFS's 63 MB/s comes from a far deeper queue, the bound's trade-off is real. 0.90.107 (36AE...) the same write: 134 cuts, win 5.6-6.5 MiB, lat_max 3197 ms, 17.4 MB/s (tests/evidence/lone-writer-ioq-0.90.107.log). HYPOTHESIS H5: the window cuts on any single completion over the target, and ~1/3 of completions at <=16 MiB exceed 500 ms, so it settles far below the depth where the TYPICAL completion reaches 500 ms; cutting on an 8-completion moving average lets it settle near that depth (~35 MB/s by the fit, inside 2x XFS) with coordination waits still ~the target. Testing: 0.90.108 EWMA cut, tests/pve_drbd_window_ab.sh ARMS=32768:500 LAPS=2; pass = lone >= 31.5 MB/s (2x of XFS's 63) and flood verdict PASS with swap max not above 0.90.105's 4.5/4.7 s. ===== H5 DISPROVEN, change reverted: 0.90.108 with the window cutting on an 8-completion moving average (6891CD8E4AA95061F349A53 on PVE), tests/pve_drbd_window_ab.sh ARMS=32768:500 LAPS=2 (tests/evidence/pve_drbd_window_ab/20261008T223931Z): lone 2 GiB 22.6 / 19.9 MB/s (pass line was 31.5), flood rc=0 both laps with swaps max 3356 / 2718 ms (lap 1) and 2821 / 2655 ms (lap 2). Re-read of the histogram: across 4-16 MiB in flight the rate is flat at ~17-25 MB/s (latency proportional to depth), so no window inside a 500 ms target buys rate on this pair; raw DRBD needs a far deeper queue (11 MB/s at 2 MiB, 48-52 MB/s at 64 MiB in flight, CHANGELOG 0.90.81), which is the depth the user's ruling declined for the heartbeat's margin. What could change the trade: coordination writes that do not queue behind the data stream at all (a separate replicated path for the disklock/ledger area), so the data window can be deep. Not attempted.
defects.impact_why: a lone writer runs at half XFS-on-DRBD speed; every byte written, no error, no stall, no shutdown: pace

defects.summary: On the physical DRBD pair, pve2's clean unmount began 8 s after pve1 rejoined and spent 11.7 s before the mount even detached. The unmount wanted PR on the root inode (ino 128), which pve1 held EX. pve2 fired the BAST at +0.3 s and again at +10.6 s, retried its acquire every second (P-LKTIMEOUT-HOLDER held_ms 5806.., retries_left 48), and got PR only when pve1 released at +11.5 s, through mxfs_dlm_unlock_open rather than a BAST response. pve1's own stats line at +10.2 s shows no BAST handled at all (bast: imm=0 def=0). A node that has just rejoined either does not receive or does not act on a BAST for its root-inode EX for ~11 s.
defects.evidence: 0.90.110 build 45595CC7D1DCEC656CFE564, tests/pve_depart_wall.sh KNOB=drbd_span_waves, lap1 arm 1 (pve2 departing) 2026-10-09 00:04:46 CDT: mount_gone_ms=11731 stopped_ms=22726 (the other laps detached in 0.8 s). Departing host's log tests/evidence/pve_depart_wall/20261009T050405Z/kmsg-lap1-drbd_span_waves1-192.168.1.81.txt: BAST FIRE ino=128 target=2229895112 at +0.317 s and +10.555 s; P-LKTIMEOUT-HOLDER hmode=EX held_ms=5806/6830; process_remote_release FOUND ino=128 mode=EX at +11.500 s; P-TAUTH-LOCAL-ORPHAN-RELEASE; 'Unmounting Filesystem' at +11.713 s. Survivor's (pve1) log, same directory, -survivor.txt: dlm_unlock REMOVING ino=128 mode=EX at +11.494 via mxfs_dlm_unlock_open; 'mxfs DLM cache ... bast: imm=0 def=0' at +10.190 s.
defects.next: Find where pve1's root-inode EX came from (its mount, 8 s earlier) and why the BAST did not reach the filesystem's handler: turn on the BAST receive probes on the rejoining host and repeat a departure 5-10 s after a rejoin; check whether the handler is not yet installed (a mounting node parks what it receives) or the EX is held by a mount-time path that does not answer BASTs. ===== Reproduced on the NESTED 7.0 pair, 0.90.111 build B77BD920E9DCBDCBF9060B8, tests/evidence/pve_depart_wall/20261009T062937Z lap2 (pve9-1 departing, pve9-2 the host that rejoined the previous lap): pve9-1's PR on ino 128 queued from about -8.9 s behind pve9-2's EX (P-LKTIMEOUT-HOLDER held_ms 11407..16527, every 1.02 s); pve9-2 released at +7.70 (dlm_unlock REMOVING ino=128 mode=EX, a plain unlock: mxfs_dlm_unlock_gen funnels through mxfs_dlm_unlock_open, so that return address names no special path); pve9-1's mount left /proc/mounts at +7.9 s, 'Unmounting Filesystem' +7.75. Meanwhile pve9-1's view-change pass handed pve9-2 652 pages (+0.00..+7.85) and pve9-2 activated them one at a time on its receive thread (P-TAUTH-PAGE-MINE via=frozen-msg 39-134 per second). pve9-2's stats: bast imm=1 def=0. The departure then cost the survivor's workload a 13.2 s operation (its PR on root, asked at +9.91, waited for the departing master's teardown, which drops LOCK_REQ, until +16.49). Hypothesis to test: the BAST for root reaches pve9-2 behind the hand-off stream on the same receive thread, or its drain waits on the DRBD swap lock the activations hold; instrument BAST receive time and drain phase walls on the rejoined host. ===== MECHANISM PROVEN 0.90.111 (physical pair, tests/evidence/pve_depart_wall/20261009T074217Z lap 2, pve2 departing 100 s after pve1 rejoined): the late answer is head-of-line blocking on pve1's receive thread, not a lost BAST. Each peer has ONE receive thread (dlm/peer.c recv loop) and it processed every PAGE_HANDOFF inline, each FROZEN a ledger activation commit of 25-40 ms. pve2's view-change stream for pve1's rejoin ran 844.15-856.27 (199 pages) faster than pve1 activated it (441 frozen-msg activations 844.65-861.32), so pve1 fell ~6.7 s behind: page 4182 handed 849.71 / activated 856.28. pve2's PR request for ino 128 sat in the stream between the FROZEN of pages 4100 and 4112 (handed ~849.1) and was processed on pve1 at 855.8217, the same ms as page 4100's activation (855.8216); pve1 released its EX 14 ms later and pve2's unmount ('Unmounting Filesystem' 856.06, stop began 849.77) proceeded. 0.90.112: page hand-offs (FREEZE_REQ, FROZEN) go to their own ordered worker (v5_hrx_*, knob handoff_rx_worker), the GOODBYE drains it first, and P-RX-DISPATCH-STATS / P-HRX-STATS print receive-thread time per message type at engine stop. Verify: tests/pve_depart_wall.sh KNOB=handoff_rx_worker ARMS='0 1' WORKLOAD=1 on the physical pair.
defects.impact_why: It delays a clean unmount by ~11 s; no data is at risk and nothing hangs past the unit's bound, so it does not block the release.

defects.summary: While a peer unmounts cleanly, its receive quiesce drops LOCK_REQ from 'mounted cleared' until its GOODBYE; the survivor's requests on resources the departing node masters get no answer and wait for the membership change (GOODBYE, then local remaster), so the survivor's file operations touching those resources stall for the departing node's teardown, measured 1-5 s per departure (worst survivor create+stat 2.1-5.6 s on the 2/net/mesh/direct rig, 1.7-5.1 s on the DRBD pairs with no rejoin in the window).
defects.evidence: 0.90.111: rig tests/evidence/rig_depart_wall/20261009T071924Z (default budget): survivor slowest op 5602/3480/2903/2457 ms, teardown_drops (P-TEARDOWN-MSG-DROP, LOCK_REQ) 5/3/2/2 per departure; DRBD physical 20261009T070700Z slowest during the departure 2.1-5.5 s; nested 20261009T062937Z lap2: the survivor's PR on the root inode asked at +9.91 s was granted at +16.49 s, after the departing master's GOODBYE (+15.14 s), 8 LOCK_REQ dropped by its teardown.
defects.next: Design: let the quiesce answer a LOCK_REQ during the teardown -- grant what is compatible (the record lands on a page the departure hands or leaves to the survivor's takeover), or answer 'departing' so the requester re-routes to the successor master at once instead of waiting for GOODBYE -- with the same safety argument as the LOCK_RELEASE and FREEZE_REQ exceptions (no local lock state, no XFS re-entry). Measure with tests/rig_depart_wall.sh and tests/pve_depart_wall.sh WORKLOAD=1: survivor slowest op during a departure under 1 s.
defects.impact_why: a 1-5 s stall of the survivor's operations per peer departure; nothing errors or hangs

defects.summary: A ledger page PREPARED by an incarnation that has since left (its authority dead) to a target that never consumed it stays PREPARED when that target dies too: the dead target's recovery takeover takes only pages whose AUTHORITY is the departed incarnation (dlm_takeover_scan_cb), the orphan sweep that judges every authority ran at mount while the target was still live ('a live target consumes it') and is not run again, and the hand-off tick retargets only pages whose authority is this node
defects.evidence: physical pair, 0.90.113 90F3B8C7A0429182B10498B, tests/pve_pair_failover.sh withdraw-p1 05:11-05:20 CDT: after pve2's recovery takeover ran (P-DEPART-WORK-RECOVERY-TAKEOVER node=3877909573 queued_ms=160916 total_ms=16715, no pages skipped), 4 pages (5237, 5245, 5263, 5297) still state=PREPARED auth=3601257097 (pve1's incarnation before the deploy's restart, gone) target=3877909573 (pve2's incarnation that withdrew)
defects.next: Queue the orphan sweep after a recovery takeover (the sweep judges every authority against the slot map and retargets a PREPARED page whose target is dead), then verify with the end-of-step census in tests/pve_pair_failover.sh on a withdraw that follows a clean restart
defects.impact_why: no hang, failure or corruption measured from it: a request on such a page is served by an on-demand takeover. Same class as the takeover-skip defect (a page left under dead authorities), one of the conditions of the rejoiner-admission deadlock

defects.summary: An AG lock's no-queue request whose master is the PEER waits a whole attempt (MXFS_LOCK_ACQUIRE_WAIT_MS, 1 s) when the master does not answer in time, and the allocator's trylock pass tries AG after AG that way while holding the VM image's ILOCK: 5-6 s per pass. The master answers a remote request from process_remote_request, which runs dlm_ledger_prepare(nowait=false) and any grant's durable ledger commit before it sends anything.
defects.evidence: Physical pair, 0.90.116 4A6E59A3DFECE4A46BBCFB5, Kingston leg tests/evidence/pve_build_leg_kmsg/20261010T081150Z-fix-0.90.116-attempt3: pve1 logged P-ACQ-NOQUEUE-UNANSWERED 61 times, all master=pve2 (1681743862, master_live=1), comm iou-wrk-242866 (38) / iou-wrk-242628 (23), in runs one second apart over ag=35,36,37,38,39,42 (e.g. 03:22:30-03:22:35 CDT; 03:25:35-39; 03:27:10-14; 03:28:22-26), about 11 such passes. pve2 logged none toward pve1. No hung task (each pass < 30 s), 7/7 installs.
defects.next: Instrument the master: per remote no-queue AG request, receipt-to-answer wall split into receive-queue delay, dlm_ledger_prepare, the decision and the grant commit (and whether the answer was a grant or a would-block), on pve2 during a Kingston leg. Then fix where the time is: a remote no-queue request on an unready page answered would-block at once with the page marked for mxfs_dlm_prepare_wanted (as 0.90.116 does locally), and/or a no-queue request's answer not held behind other requests' commits on the receive thread. ===== Instrument (0.90.116 scratch build 9E2B45A38495224AE267A4A): P-RREQ-NOQUEUE-SLOW on the master for every peer no-queue AG request answered in >= 250 ms, with prepare_ms (dlm_ledger_prepare) and rest_ms (decision + any grant commit). Three hypotheses, decided by the Kingston leg: H-R1 prepare_ms dominates (the page is not ready on the master: fix as 0.90.116 did locally); H-R2 rest_ms dominates (the grant's durable commit, or waiting for table locks); H-R3 the master answers fast (no P-RREQ line near a requester's P-ACQ-NOQUEUE-UNANSWERED) -- the request waited in the master's receive queue behind other messages, or the answer in the requester's. ===== Instrument leg (pair build B8B3EF5DD378D9F35DC5E7B, tests/evidence/pve_build_leg_kmsg/*rreq-instrument-0.90.116): pve2 49 / pve1 15 unanswered no-queue AG tries; on the masters P-RREQ-NOQUEUE-SLOW 24 (pve1) / 1 (pve2), every one rc=0 (a GRANT, answered after its durable ledger commit), wall 255-11319 ms, prepare_ms 0 in most, rest_ms dominant (9 of the 10 that match an unanswered try); 39 of pve2's 49 unanswered tries match NO slow processing on pve1 -- they waited behind earlier requests on pve1's single per-peer receive thread (e.g. 04:32:37-43 ag 9,11,13,16,20,21 answered back to back after a 3698 ms one). H-R2 + H-R3 hold, H-R1 marginal. Fix candidate 1 (requester): dl_noqueue_remote_wait_ms (200; 1000 = old) bounds the no-queue AG try's wait; a late grant is adopted by the kept (gave_up) acquisition record for the next try. Predictions for a Kingston leg vs the instrument leg: no trylock run of ~1 s waits (each unanswered costs <= 0.2 s), P958-ACQ-GRANT-CLAIMED > 0 and at least P958-ACQ-GRANT-RELEASED why=idle, installs 7/7 and flush means no worse. The master-side cause (grant commits run inline on the per-peer receive thread, head-of-line) stays to be fixed separately. ===== Fix candidate 1 DISPROVEN and removed: dl_noqueue_remote_wait_ms=200 (build DBF6C2F1AB31CC5881E7E85, tests/evidence/pve_build_leg_kmsg/*rwait200-0.90.116) -- unanswered tries 33+32 (control 15+49), late grants P958-ACQ-GRANT-CLAIMED 2+2 vs P958-ACQ-GRANT-RELEASED 13+23 (most late grants were handed back unused: two wasted durable commits each on the master), installs pve1 2447-2493 s pve2 1955-2217 s (control 2363-2403 / 1946-2147), guest write means pve2 779-1072 ms (control 642-887), flush 48-57 ms (control 44-53). Shortening the wait moves the cost onto the master. New hypothesis H-R5: the master's receive thread serves a peer's LOCK_REQ/LOCK_RELEASE inline, each grant or release a durable commit, so a cheap answer (a would-block deny, a fast grant) waits behind another resource's slow commit (39 of 49 unanswered tries matched no slow processing on the master). Fix: master-side messages (LOCK_REQ, LOCK_RELEASE, LOCK_CANCEL) on workers sharded by resource, FIFO per shard (per-resource order kept), drained before a GOODBYE; knob for A/B. Prediction: unanswered no-queue tries fall to about the count whose own grant commit is slow (~10 of 49), installs and guest latency no worse. ===== 0.90.117 legs, physical pair, Kingston spare disks, 7 installs. (1) Request workers only (03981811, tests/evidence/pve_build_leg_kmsg/20261010T131113Z-rrq-workers-0.90.117): P-ACQ-NOQUEUE-UNANSWERED 120+60 vs 61-65 total on three 0.90.116 legs; P-RREQ-NOQUEUE-SLOW shows the master's time in rest_ms (decision + grant commit: pve2 256-12612 ms, prepare_ms 0 on all 37); P-RRQ-STATS max_wait_ms 29430/39207 in the worker queues; unanswered tries come in runs of up to 36 consecutive AGs, 1 s each, from one thread; 84 late grants adopted unclaimed and released. The receive-thread head-of-line hypothesis is DISPROVEN. (2) Workers + dropping no-queue requests that waited past MXFS_LOCK_ACQUIRE_WAIT_MS (8AF4E4F7, .../20261010T141420Z-drop-stale-noqueue-0.90.117): unanswered 23+43 (back to the 0.90.116 level, not below), late grants released 8+9, 40 stale requests dropped, worker max_wait 13387/5310 ms, slowest installs 2365/2045 s. STILL OPEN: the master's decide+commit takes seconds and the requester still spends a whole 1 s attempt per remote-master AG under the ILOCK. Next hypothesis to test: after one unanswered no-queue AG try toward a master, the same allocation pass should not spend another full attempt on each further AG that master owns (answer would-block at once for that master for the rest of the pass); measure the run lengths of P-ACQ-NOQUEUE-UNANSWERED and the per-pass time under the ILOCK before and after. ===== 0.90.118 (hypothesis H-R6, tested): the requester's cost is the run, not the single try. Mined from the three legs above (tests/evidence/pve_build_leg_kmsg/*{drop-stale-noqueue-0.90.117,rrq-workers-0.90.117,rreq-instrument-0.90.116}/kmsg-*.txt): 310 P-ACQ-NOQUEUE-UNANSWERED, all type=3 (AG), all comm iou-wrk-*, each file one master; 117 runs per thread (gap <= 1.6 s), 231 of 310 tries (75%) came straight after another unanswered try from the same thread toward the same master, runs up to 25 AGs (rrq-workers pve1 08:32:52 iou-wrk-355734 ags 38..23). Change: once a master leaves one of an allocation's no-queue AG tries unanswered, the rest of that allocation (xfs_alloc_arg.mxfs_mute_master, kept across every AG walk and pass made with those args) answers would-block at once for AGs that master owns (P-AGNB-MUTED), without sending; knob ag_nb_mute_unanswered_master (1; 0 = old). Instrument: P-ALLOC-WALK-SLOW per AG walk >= 1 s (ms, got, mute). Predictions for A/B arm 1 vs arm 0 on one build, Kingston leg, 7 installs: unanswered tries fall to about the number of runs (~1 per allocation per master, under ~35% of arm 0's count); P-ALLOC-WALK-SLOW walks of >= 3 s vanish in arm 1 (arm 0 shows them); installs 7/7, no bad lines, install times and guest write latency no worse. Falsified if arm 1's unanswered count is not well below arm 0's, or arm 1 still shows multi-second walks, or installs regress. ===== 0.90.118 A/B on one build (076200B2F7C1F961F0139E8), physical pair, Kingston legs, 7 installs each, arm 1 first: tests/evidence/pve_build_leg_kmsg/20261010T174522Z-ag_nb_mute_unanswered_master-1-1 (knob 1) and tests/evidence/pve_build_leg_kmsg/20261010T183502Z-ag_nb_mute_unanswered_master-0-2 (knob 0). Unanswered no-queue tries 8+6 vs 80+31 (P-AGNB-MUTE-STATS muted 24+59 vs 0); P-ALLOC-WALK-SLOW walks >= 1 s 12+10 vs 28+16, longest 4.9/8.5 s vs 46.1/16.5 s; installs pve1 2308-2463 s vs 2662-2698 s, pve2 1938-2151 vs 2139-2451 (arm order not alternated). ARM 0 HUNG: 13:46:54 CDT pve1 hung-task reports for 14 tasks; the holder named by the kernel is iou-wrk-448623:450229 (state S) in xfs_alloc_vextent_iterate_ags -> mxfs_ag_dlm_trylock_alloc -> mxfs_dlm_lock_noqueue -> pending_wait, holding the image ILOCK while AGs 51..57,2,3 (all master pve2) each went unanswered one second apart; its walk ended at 46119 ms. So the defect crosses the stability bar without the fix. Predictions held for arm 1 (unanswered fell ~87%, no multi-ten-second walk). Not yet FIXED AND VERIFIED: arm 1 had its own hung-task episode with an unidentified holder (D-DRBD-GUEST-WRITE-ILOCK-HOLDER-UNKNOWN-30S-0-90-118); repeat legs needed, alternating arm order. ===== Second A/B, arms reversed (0 first), build E8B6C853D1BD97C4133E304 with P-ILOCK-HOLD-SLOW: tests/evidence/pve_build_leg_kmsg/20261010T205026Z-ag_nb_mute_unanswered_master-0-1 PASS (unanswered 34+23, P-ALLOC-WALK-SLOW 17+8, P-ILOCK-HOLD-SLOW 2+1 at 16834/16991/16223 ms, each equal to that allocation's walk ms: the hold IS the walk) and tests/evidence/pve_build_leg_kmsg/20261010T213954Z-ag_nb_mute_unanswered_master-1-2 PASS (unanswered 11+3, muted 29+20, walks 13+4, P-ILOCK-HOLD-SLOW 0). Installs favour the first arm in both A/Bs (Kingston drift), so install times do not rank the arms. Across both A/Bs the fix removes every >= 10 s image-ILOCK hold seen and cuts unanswered tries 75-87%. Not closed: arm 1 of the first A/B still had D-DRBD-GUEST-WRITE-ILOCK-HOLDER-UNKNOWN-30S-0-90-118. USER DIRECTIVE 2026-10-10: no more legs on the 2011 Kingston SVP100S (being removed); the next verification runs on the pair's Samsung 850 EVOs, where whether this reproduces at all is the first question.
defects.impact_why: USER RULING 2026-10-10: attributed to faulty hardware, so it does not block a release. Every observation is on pve1/pve2's Kingston SSDNow V+ SVP100S (2011 SATA, pulled from a decommissioned server after ~5 years in service, ~10 years ago), which stall ~1 s per flush for minutes even on the raw device with no filesystem (tests/pve_small_write_stall.sh); never observed on the Samsung 850 EVOs, the iSCSI LUN or the nested pair. The record stays OPEN: this is a scoping decision, not a disposition, and any observation on other hardware restores the stability bar.

defects.summary: A mount's outbound peer handshake read failed with -104 (ECONNRESET) and was logged at error level ('peer: handshake reply from node N failed: -104', dlm/peer.c:920-929), on a join that then completed normally.
defects.evidence: Physical pair pve1/pve2, 0.90.116 build 4A6E59A3DFECE4A46BBCFB5 (PVE 6.17 kernel), 2026-10-10 07:25 CDT: systemctl start mxfs-drbd@mxfssdb on both hosts at once while /mnt/shared (resource mxfs) was already mounted on both. pve2 kernel: [55883.992561] 'mxfs: peer: handshake reply from node 1852801132 failed: -104' then [55883.992642] 'P-JOIN-INSTALLED node=902241850 peer=1852801132 attempts=1 ms=118'. Both resources then Primary/Primary UpToDate, both mounted. journalctl -k over all retained boots on both hosts: 1 occurrence ever (pve1 0, pve2 1); pve1 logged 12 P-JOIN-INSTALLED this boot with no such line. Cause not established: the reading that both sides connected at once and one reset the duplicate (or that SO_REUSEPORT routed the connect to the other volume's listener, which reset it instead of replying with its volume_id, as peer.c:943-958 expects) is unproven; the accept side logs at debug only.
defects.next: Enable dyndbg for dlm/peer.c on both hosts, restart mxfs-drbd@mxfssdb on both at once repeatedly with mxfs mounted, and capture the accept side's decision for the reset connection (crossed-connect dedupe vs wrong-volume listener). If it is the dedupe, the outbound path must recognise that outcome rather than report a failure; if it is the wrong listener, that listener must reply with its volume_id so the -EAGAIN path runs. ===== ===== 2026-10-17 (session 41) CAUSE READ IN THE CODE (to be proven on a lap): the host's shared TCP port routes every connection by the volume its NODE_JOIN names (pal/linux/kern.c mxfs_tcp_port_acceptor peeks the NODE_JOIN, mxfs_tcp_port_route); one for a volume no mount there listens for yet is sock_release()d with the peeked NODE_JOIN still unread ('pal: port %u: a connection for no filesystem mounted here; closed', DEBUG), and closing a socket with unread data resets it, so the connector's reply read (dlm/peer.c) returns -104 and logged it at ERR. Starting both hosts' mounts of mxfssdb at once while mxfs was mounted makes the first connect beat the peer's own mxfssdb listener. Neither earlier reading (crossed-connect dedupe; SO_REUSEPORT to the wrong listener) fits: the accept side replies before it looks at any existing connection, and routing is by volume key, not SO_REUSEPORT. CHANGE WRITTEN (main tree, not built): dlm/peer.c logs a reply-read -ECONNRESET at INFO ('peer: node N reset the handshake: its host has no mount of this volume listening yet (or the connection was lost); retrying on the next discovery'), any other reply-read failure still at ERR; return value unchanged. HARNESS: tests/multi_mount.sh MM_SIMUL_B=<cycles> unmounts B on every member and mounts it on all at once per cycle; the scan reports per node handshake ERR lines (FAIL), 'reset the handshake' lines and the router's 'a connection for no filesystem mounted here; closed' lines. NEXT: control on a build without the change (e.g. ~/src/mxfs-e 737E182A) and fix on a sibling built from the main tree, MM_SIMUL_B=10, tcp, test18 test19: REPRODUCED = an ERR -104 within 1 s of the peer's unrouted close; FIXED = zero ERR handshake lines, every reset paired with a peer close, every mount rc=0, all leases ACTIVE. ===== ===== 2026-10-17 (session 42) A/B QUEUE WRITTEN AND RUN; ITS FIRST RUN MEASURED NOTHING (HARNESS DEFECT, FIXED); RERUNNING. Queue tests/queues/join_handshake_reset_ab.queue (rules written first): control = ~/src/mxfs-e 737E182A809291DAA0B4785 (reset at ERR), fix = ~/src/mxfs-c 9E03AF016F66F5400C65EBF (reset at INFO), the builds differ in dlm/peer.c and dlm/dlm_caw.c only (diff -rq of xfs dlm pal mxfs_clayer compat include); MM_SIMUL_B=10 tcp test18 test19, control/fix/control/fix; CONTROL REPRODUCED = a -104 reply failure on a node whose peer logged an unrouted close in the run; FIX PASS = harness PASS, >= 1 'reset the handshake' line, each node's resets <= its peer's unrouted closes; FIXED AND VERIFIED needs one control REPRODUCED and both fix PASS. defects.summary: fence=quorum on the shared attachment lets a node frozen by its hypervisor HOST keep writing after the survivor took it over. The survivor's kind-30 certificate (the loser ended its boot) is false: the loser never resets. While the nested ESXi host is paused, commands the guest handed to ESXi stay queued, and on unpause ESXi issues them. The guest's clock did not advance across the pause, so its 3 s quorum lease still read valid, and it issued new writes. Its corosync merged back into the membership without ever reporting it inquorate. It stopped only when its heartbeat found its slot taken over (P290-AUTH-WITHDRAW reason=SLOT_TAKEOVER), 0.85 s of guest time after resume.
defects.evidence: tests/vsphere_shared_fence.sh freeze host, build CC54CCA6EE7210901855D5B, vstest1/vstest2 on the physical RDM (eui.6661313331363962), qnetd on serv. vstest2 writes O_DIRECT stamped 4 KiB blocks from 16 threads; vmrun pause esxhost2; vstest1 took over at +75 s (P238-SHARED-FENCE-ENDED kind=30 obs=quorum-loser-deadline-passed, foreign replay, P163-RECOVERY-COMPLETE); snapshot A; unpause; snapshot B differs in 4 blocks: 785, 878 and 1623 stamped 32.92-32.94 s (queued in ESXi at the pause), and 1639 (thread 7, seq 614) stamped 33.77 s, a new write 0.83 s of guest time after seq 613. Afterwards vstest2 was still on boot 5095e60e (the certified-ended one), quorate=1, member=1, mounted, FS shut down at [33.92]. The guest-suspend control (govc vm.power -suspend, quorum-10-freeze-guest): no late write; vSphere's suspend drains I/O.
defects.next: No in-guest mechanism can stop this. Queued commands are below the guest, and a resumed guest cannot see its freeze before it writes. Fix by putting a storage barrier under the vote: (1) refuse fence=quorum on a device with no SCSI persistent reservations (a multi-writer VMDK answers PR with invalid opcode), the same way fence=scsipr is refused there; (2) on a physical RDM (PR forwarded per guest, one VM per host), register a key at arm and hold a WEAR reservation, and have the survivor PREEMPT AND ABORT the victim's key before replay, so that late commands get RESERVATION CONFLICT. Verify with freeze host repeated, zero late writes, and the kill/split/restart laps.
defects.impact_why: Measured: 4 blocks of the victim's file changed on disk after the survivor had certified its boot ended and replayed its slice (tests/evidence/vsphere/quorum-11-freeze-host/late_writes.txt).

defects.next: Find where load_module spends the ~0.9 s without a reschedule (function_graph or perf on a guest during insmod: relocation, ftrace/alternatives patching, kallsyms, or module init) and break it up; then re-measure with tests/module_load_stall.sh (target: longest gap well under 0.5 s). ===== ===== 2026-10-17 (session 33) FIRST PROFILE: THE TRACED CHILDREN OF load_module ACCOUNT FOR ~170 MS OF ~1.28 S. New harness tests/module_load_profile.sh <node> [depth] [thresh_us] (function_graph, set_graph_function=load_module, tracing_thresh; debug-stripped module; tracer reset after). Run on test5 (6.8.0-101-generic, 2 vCPU, main-tree build 3AEA31FDF4AD31EFBBA6A90 stripped to 11822576 bytes, force_transport=1), depth 4, thresh 5000 us: insmod_ms=1304, load_module 1277496 us; calls >= 5 ms: blocking_notifier_call_chain_robust 113270 us (static_call_module_notify 56457, jump_label_module_notify 7332), post_relocation 22873 (module_finalize 21599, apply_returns 19714), text_poke_queue 10016 (text_poke_bp_batch 10009), do_init_module 12095 (init_xfs_fs 6895), layout_and_allocate 6619 (move_module 5639), mod_sysfs_setup 6160 (module_param_sysfs_setup 5758). The remaining ~1.1 s is spent inline in load_module or in many calls each under 5 ms (candidates: simplify_symbols/resolve_symbol per undefined symbol, apply_relocations per RELA section, ftrace_module_init, dynamic_debug_setup, the module's 790 parameters). NEXT: the same harness at depth 2 with thresh 0 (raise buffer_size_kb) and sum durations by function name to name the stretch; then decide what MXFS can change (fewer relocations or symbols, an init split, cond_resched in its own init) versus what is the kernel's load path. ===== ===== 2026-10-17 (session 36) THE STRETCH IS NAMED: ftrace's per-record kallsyms lookup, records x symbols. tests/module_load_profile.sh test5 2 0 (depth 2, no threshold; main-tree build 3AEA31FD stripped to 11822576 bytes, 6.8.0-101-generic, 2 vCPU; trace kept at tests/evidence/module_load_profile/20261017T1713Z_test5_d2t0.txt): insmod_ms=1507, load_module 1341.8 ms, of which kallsyms_lookup 5750 calls 989.1 ms, blocking_notifier_call_chain_robust 128.7 ms, text_poke_queue 5750 calls 70.9 ms, do_init_module 12.5 ms, find_symbol 272 calls 9.4 ms, mod_sysfs_setup 6.8 ms (durations are tracer upper bounds). 5750 is exactly mxfs.ko's fentry record count (__mcount_loc 0xb3b0 bytes / 8). Code (upstream /src/linux 7.1, kernel/trace/ftrace.c): ftrace_module_enable walks every record of the module and calls test_for_valid_rec -> kallsyms_lookup(rec->ip) (ftrace.c:4338-4352, :7982; x86 defines FTRACE_MCOUNT_MAX_OFFSET, arch/x86/include/asm/ftrace.h:18), and a module address lookup is find_kallsyms_symbol, a linear scan of the module's whole symtab (kernel/module/kallsyms.c:253-298). mxfs.ko has 29634 named symbols (nm: T 8581, t 5932, r 5816, d 5337, D 1543, b 1151, B 580, R 99; 4166 are static locals named x.NNN, chiefly _rs 876 ratelimit states, __func__ 711, descriptor 633), so the load costs ~5750 x ~29000 symbol visits. Verify both records with the same log evidence. ===== 2026-10-17 KEPT-LOG SWEEP: 19 P-ACQ-NOQUEUE-UNANSWERED lines with master_live=0 in kept path_* rows (2/4/8/16 nodes, 2026-10-05..15), every such row PASS. NEXT before removal: read whether a remounting node's new ctx ever purges (or should clear) its own predecessor's shadow entries on the volume; if not, the change must also end a predecessor incarnation's entries at mount (the volume's entries owned by any incarnation of this node other than the current one), then a lap set with the test18 variant reached in a control and absent in the fix. ===== 2026-10-19 (session 118) CODE READ (main tree): the shadow is one static table per module (dlm/dlm.c dg_shadow[DG_SHADOW_N]); ctx->dg_volume/dg_volume_set are per context; nothing clears an entry when a context ends: mxfs_dlm_destroy (dlm/dlm.c:8195) frees the lock table only, dg_release_owner runs only from dlm_purge_node_impl (a dead PEER), dg_release only on a genuine release by its owner. So a node that unmounts and mounts again (the fenced victim rejoining under a new node id, the module kept loaded) starts its new context over every EX its previous context's shadow left active - its own grants as master (owner = its previous node id) and holders that later released while another node mastered the resource - and its first EX grant of such a resource prints P-DOUBLEGRANT naming them: the test18 variant of dgc2 (its own predecessor) and dgf2a (test17's old incarnation 2351111129). HYPOTHESIS H-DG2 (written before the patch is measured): ending every active entry of the volume when the context ends removes the rejoined node's P-DOUBLEGRANT reports. CHANGE (main tree, not yet built or measured): dg_release_volume(ctx), called first in mxfs_dlm_destroy under table_rwlock, clears active on every entry of ctx->dg_volume (last_owner and the handoff epoch untouched, as dg_release_owner does), logs P-DG-DESTROY-RELEASED local= n=; knob dl_dg_destroy_releases (1 default, 0 = the same-build control). NEXT: a build carrying it (it also carries dl_dead_sender_drop, D-MASTER-OWN's change: keep that at its default 1 in both arms), path_fenced_return laps on 2/net/mesh/mpath g2e alternating dl_dg_destroy_releases=0/1 with dl_dg_purge_releases=1, every lap on a fresh prep so the shadow starts empty and the variant can only come from that lap's own fenced context; count per node P-DOUBLEGRANT whose owner_existing is a previous incarnation of the logging node or of its peer, and dg_doublegrant_n. SUPPORTED: the variant in at least one control lap and in no fix lap; chk_clean CLEAN and the row PASS in every lap. ===== 2026-10-19 (session 119) H-DG2 A/B WRITTEN, NOT YET RUN: tests/queues/dg_destroy_releases_ab_netmesh_mpath.queue (rules in its header, written before any lap; copied into ~/src/mxfs-e), 8 laps alternating dl_dg_destroy_releases=0/1 on ~/src/mxfs-e (A4C1E0DA75665C882237C4E), dl_dead_sender_drop and dl_dg_purge_releases at their default 1, 2/net/mesh/mpath g2e, each on a fresh prep; graded by tools/dead_sender_ab_grade.py (VARIANT = the rejoined victim's P-DOUBLEGRANT naming its own fenced node id, DESTROYED = its P-DG-DESTROY-RELEASED lines; both print because prep loads the module with dyndbg=+p). Launch from ~/src/mxfs-e as lap_queue label dgd once queue dsd (D-MASTER-OWN, same build, started 10:23:33Z, ~12 x 8-10 min) is DONE. Supporting data meanwhile: every dsd lap runs with dl_dg_destroy_releases=1; dsd lap 1 (dsdc1, run 20261019T102505Z-g2e) read shadow test18 f0 destroy1 (no variant, the release ran), against queue ors's 30-56 variant reports per lap on a build without the change. ===== 2026-10-19 (session 1c324e00) dgd LAUNCHED 12:35:12Z from ~/src/mxfs-e (A4C1E0DA75665C882237C4E) on g2e per tests/queues/dg_destroy_releases_ab_netmesh_mpath.queue, then STOPPED for the 0.90.131 release run, which needs every rig VM: lap 1 dgdc1 (C) ran (run 20261019T123648Z-g2e: path_fenced_return PASS 213/400 s, alloc_witness PASS, chk_clean PASS verdict=CLEAN release=CLEAN errors=0), lap 2 dgdf1 (F) ran to its end at 12:50Z, the queue runner was terminated after it, and lap 3 dgdc2 was cut by the release chain's rig power-down at 12:52Z.
