defects.summary: A shared LUN with 4096-byte logical blocks (4K-native, what most new arrays present) cannot be formatted: mkfs.mxfs fails at its first write, and every on-disk layout and I/O path assumes 512-byte logical blocks.
defects.evidence: 2026-10-19 (session 1c324e00), tests/fourkn_lun.sh + tests/fourkn_mount_probe.sh, log tests/evidence/fourkn_20261019.log: an SCST vdisk_fileio LUN with blocksize=4096 bound to test31/test32 (blockdev --getss 4096, --getpbsz 4096). Published 0.90.130 (v0.90.130 source rebuilt to srcversion 1E9C0DE7364AD47BCDDE54A, the release's) and the 0.90.131 release build (8DAEC6B8298ADB049222D74) both: 'mkfs.mxfs: pwrite at offset 4096 failed: Invalid argument', rc=1, at the journal superblock, the first write (a 512-byte O_DIRECT pwrite, tools/mkfs_mxfs.c write_sectors called with 512 bytes from format_journal); both mounts then refused 'Invalid superblock magic number'. Nothing is written before the failure. The 512-byte assumption is everywhere (scout, raw file:line): mkfs writes XFS sectsize 512 (tools/mkfs_mxfs.c:97, :1004) and log sectsize 0; MXFS_JOURNAL_SECTOR_SIZE 512 (dlm/journal.h:57); the per-sector SCSI COMPARE AND WRITE sends LBA = byte offset / 512, 1 block, 1024 bytes (pal/linux/kern.c:8406-8421, caw_manual_bio :8221, :8242) with no block-size check; only the whole-page swap checks bdev_logical_block_size == 512 (:8683); dlm/mount.c:1913 a 1024-byte CAW buffer; MXFS_TAUTH_ROOT_BYTES 512; tools/mxfs_admin.c:205 refuses sectsize != 512. The rig has only ever served 512-byte LUNs (scripts/scst_setup.sh:54 blocksize=512). UNEXPLAINED: a tester (gyptazy.com blog, 0.90.130, fdisk 'Sector size (logical/physical): 4096 bytes / 16384 bytes') reported mkfs.mxfs 'formatted successfully' through every region; a 512-byte O_DIRECT write on a device whose kernel logical block size is 4096 cannot succeed, and their mount output is not shown.
defects.next: 1. Fail closed with the cause: mkfs.mxfs (BLKSSZGET) and the mount (bdev_logical_block_size of the device) refuse a logical block size other than 512 with a message naming it, so no layout written for 512 can ever be mounted on a 4K-native device. 2. Learn what the tester's kernel saw: blockdev --getss and --getpbsz on their /dev/sdc and their mount output. 3. 4K-native support, design written first: the format's sector size, the journal sector, the disklock and ledger units and the CAW unit all taken from the device's logical block size; then a rig LUN of each size in the release matrix (scripts/scst_setup.sh blocksize) so both are verified. ===== 2026-10-19 (session 1c324e00) OWNER DECISION: 4K-native support is NOT in 0.90.131 (it ships refusing 4K-native LUNs at format, as 0.90.130 does); it is the work of 0.90.132. Approved: write the 4K-native design first (docs/, before any patch): sector size from the device at format; every structure two nodes write independently (disklock slots, journal slot headers, recovery manifests, authority-ledger roots, PR registrant and bootstrap records) in a logical block of its own, never a shared 4 KiB block (a read-modify-write of a shared block between nodes is corruption); CAW LBA, block count and buffers in device logical blocks (pal/linux/kern.c caw_manual_bio and callers); tools (chk_mxfs, resize_mxfs, mxfs_admin, caw_verify); 512-byte devices keep today's layout. First deliverable of 0.90.132: mkfs and mount refuse a logical block size other than 512 with a message naming it. Then a 4096-byte rig LUN class (scripts/scst_setup.sh blocksize) in the release matrix.
defects.impact_why: Measured on a 4096-byte-logical LUN: 0.90.130 and 0.90.131 mkfs refuse at the first write (nothing written) and the mount refuses the unformatted device; no data written, no node stopped. A functional gap, not a crossing of the integrity or stability bar.

defects.summary: mkfs.mxfs prints sizes in GiB labelled GB (human_size divides by 1024^3 and prints 'GB'), so a 100 GiB LUN reads as '99.37 GB usable' and looks 7 GB short.
defects.evidence: tools/mkfs_mxfs.c:264 snprintf(buf, buflen, "%.2f GB", (double)bytes / (1024.0 * 1024 * 1024)); a tester (gyptazy.com, 0.90.130) read '99.37 GB at offset 672296960' on a 107374182400-byte LUN as about 7 GB unexplained; the true difference is the 0.63 GiB envelope.
defects.next: Label GiB/MiB/KiB in human_size (and the other size prints in tools/), next version: a tools source change during the 0.90.131 verification would make the packaged mkfs differ from the one verified.
defects.impact_why: A wrong unit label in mkfs output; nothing written or read differs.

defects.summary: The F4 committed-never-submitted registry never sees a successful FUA write of a bmbt buffer: on a multi-node mount every bmbt write takes the FUA arm of xfs_buf_submit_ex (pal/linux/xfs_buf.c:13645-13649), which on success completes through xfs_buf_ioend and returns at :13796, before xfs_buf_submit_bio (:13803) where mxfs_f4_submit stamps submit_gen (:8956). So a directory bmbt leaf written by FUA keeps submit_gen 0, its completion leaves the record open (xfs/xfs_mxfs_obligation.c:550), and the registry reports it committed-never-submitted: P285-F4-BLI-FREED-OPEN, P285-F4-REC truth=GEN-OPEN-NOT-DIRTY, P491-REL-UNDEST f4_open, P286-F4-ORPHAN and the orphan counter at unmount, all false for these buffers. With f4_gate=0 (default) the count changes nothing (relbar census-and-proceed :479-500, certificate counters :1072-1075, cause tags :706-711, P491-REL-UNDEST probe only, and the evict shutdown condition xfs_mxfs_evict.c:562-563 leaves f4_open out); it makes the telemetry unable to show a real committed-never-submitted directory buffer and would make f4_gate=1 defer every release of a btree directory after such a write.
defects.evidence: 0.90.131 release chain window lap 7 (run 20261019T140254Z, build 8DAEC6B8298ADB049222D74), test1 kernel ring tests/evidence/w2laps_0.90.131_dmesg_test1_140918Z.gz: P285-F4-BLI-FREED-OPEN lines 2080 (daddr 25850600 committed_gen 3512), 5939 (24784056, 3807), 12099 (24784056, 4312); P491-REL-UNDEST line 15112 (ino=25165952 held_mode=5 f4_open=2 comm=kworker/u5:15); P285-F4-REC truth=GEN-OPEN-NOT-DIRTY bli=0 dirty=0 in_ail=0 delwri=0 submit_gen=0 lines 26331-26332 (3646.40); P286-F4-ORPHAN lines 73137-73138 under umount (3759.44); F4-REGISTRY-TOTAL line 73141. Against a lost commit: the last P66-LEAFWRITE of both leaves (3637.287, numrecs 170+167) equals the in-core extent count (P62-IFLUSH-FORCE if_nextents=337 leafsum=337 at 3637.309), after the newest commit (gen 4312 by 3634.5) and before the release at 3641.1. Contradiction left open: that write is xfs_bwrite of the cached leaf (xfs/xfs_mxfs_dir_bmbt.c:1116-1126), whose submit should stamp submit_gen (pal/linux/xfs_buf.c:8956, mxfs_f4_submit) and whose completion should retire the record, yet the record read submit_gen=0 nine seconds later. Not audited: window laps run no chk_clean and the next lap reformats the LUN.
defects.next: Stamp the F4 submit on the bmbt FUA arm (call mxfs_f4_submit(bp) before mxfs_buf_write_fua at pal/linux/xfs_buf.c ~13698, so the success completion at :13795 retires the record), then show on the rig that a FUA-written directory bmbt leaf retires its record (P286-F4-ORPHAN 0 and F4-REGISTRY-TOTAL orphans=0 at unmount on a 2/net/mesh/mpath path_fenced_return lap), and that a real committed-never-submitted buffer still opens one. Not in 0.90.131: a source change restarts its validation.
defects.impact_why: Measured on 0.90.131 window lap 7 (tests/evidence/w2laps_0.90.131_dmesg_test1_140918Z.gz): both leaves the registry held open were written by successful FUA writes after their newest commit (P63-LEAFWR owner=25165952 daddr=24784056 numrecs=170 rc=0 and daddr=25850600 numrecs=167 rc=0 at 3637.3086, the FUA arm print; 170+167 = if_nextents 337; newest commit gen 4312 by 3634.5 and the record still at 4312 at 3646.4), with no P61-FUA-SKIP-BMBT, P63-BMBT-FUAWR-FALLBACK, P82, P77 or P81 for any bmbt write in the ring; and the peer, which can read that directory only after the EX release at 3641.1, then read every one of the 52998 files in it (VERIFY ok=52998 missing=0). Nothing was lost, and by the code read above the false count reaches no deferral, shutdown or replay decision with the default f4_gate=0.

defects.summary: On the 0.90.131 release build posix_multi fails at 8 and 16 nodes on both transports: rank 1's ls of the 128 test files (posix_multi.sh:56-57) meets a cached shell of a reused number for most names, each one is poisoned (P-RELOAD-XINCARN-POISON, new in 0.90.131), and the lookup's retire waits for the revocation work's reference, queued on the inode BAST workqueue behind the drains: about 2.5 s per name.
defects.evidence: Boards: board_8-disk-caw-direct_g8_bL2_0.90.131.log:66, board_16-disk-caw-direct_g16_bL1_0.90.131.log:58, board_8-net-mesh-mpath_g8b_bL3_0.90.131.log:63, board_16-net-mesh-direct_g16_bL3_0.90.131.log:75 (FAIL posix_multi BUDGET_EXHAUSTED=1 rank 1 'step=pm own node1_file<FPN> exists', every other rank 'pm barrier count' then FAIL '... sees nodeN renamed content(exp=posix_N got=)'). On a fresh prep (tests/posix_multi_incarn_ab.sh, 8/disk/caw/direct g8, tests/evidence/20261019T164853Z_pmincarn_g8a) the row passed with lookup_dir_incarn_verify=1 in 3 s and 13 s: the stall needs dead shells left by earlier rows. H-PM1 (the lookup_dir_incarn_verify arm is the cost) REFUTED by that A/B. ===== BOARD CELLS this record accounts for (posix_multi FAIL: rank 1 BUDGET_EXHAUSTED at 'pm own node1_fileN exists', its peers' barrier checks failed): 8/disk/caw/mpath 2026-10-19T14:29:23Z (run 20261019T142249Z-g8b, board_8-disk-caw-mpath_g8b_bL1_0.90.131.log:53); 16/disk/caw/direct 2026-10-19T14:29:31Z (20261019T142249Z-g16, board_16-disk-caw-direct_g16_bL1_0.90.131.log:58); 8/net/mesh/mpath 2026-10-19T15:51:28Z (20261019T154607Z-g8b, board_8-net-mesh-mpath_g8b_bL3_0.90.131.log:63); 16/net/mesh/direct 2026-10-19T15:51:52Z (20261019T154607Z-g16, board_16-net-mesh-direct_g16_bL3_0.90.131.log:75).

Directed repro: run posix_multi repeatedly on one prep (p2 already took 13 s vs 3 s) and time rank 1's ls; build in a sibling (tools/sibling_sync.sh ~/src/mxfs-b) while main-tree queues run. ===== H-PM3 REFUTED as the stall's cause (tests/posix_multi_incarn_ab.sh KNOB=poison_revoke_idle_skip PRE_ROWS='fio_perf cache_coherency strong_consistency', 8/disk/caw/direct g8, ~/src/mxfs-b C4E512657B76E7AA7963116, console tests/evidence/pmrv_ab.console): p1_F1 PASS 3 s, p1_C0 FAIL BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, p2_F1 (switch 1) FAIL BUDGET_EXHAUSTED the same way. In p2_F1 rank 1's kernlog (~/src/mxfs-b/tests/evidence/run_posix_multi_20261019T172141Z-g8/kernlog_test7.gz:42170-42268) every name: P95-SAMETYPE-RELOAD (same mode, other generation), P-RELOAD-XINCARN-POISON aliases=0 inuse=0 dlm_mode=0 comm=ls, P-POISON-IDLE-NOREVOKE (the switch took effect), nothing for 2.4 s, P95C-SAMETYPE-WAIT resolved=0 rounds=201, then P34H-POISON-EVICT try=1 i_count=1 (retired at once) and the re-get adopts the new incarnation: 24 P95C-SAMETYPE-WAIT in the file, all resolved=0 rounds=201. The 2.4 s is the same-type resolver of xfs_lookup (xfs/xfs_inode.c, the while p95c < 200 loop) reloading a shell its first reload poisoned: it exits only when a reload clears i_dlm_stale, and a poisoned shell is never adopted in place. The same signature on 2/disk/caw/direct, tests/recreated_dir_peer_mkdir.sh rdm1 (~/src/mxfs-c/tests/evidence/20261019T172039Z_rdm_rdm1, 10 of 10 laps: P95-SAMETYPE-RELOAD, XINCARN-POISON, P95C rounds=201 2.4 s later, P34H try=1). Directed A/B running: tests/recreated_dir_peer_mkdir.sh KNOB=sametype_poison_break (peer mkdir -p timed against 195 ms, posix_multi's per-name share of its 25 s budget), ~/src/mxfs-g D92BBDD701614A7502A4308, console tests/evidence/rdm2.console; the board-shape A/B (posix_multi_incarn_ab.sh KNOB=sametype_poison_break) follows on g8. H-PM3's switch (poison_revoke_idle_skip) stays default 1 in that build and is A/B'd on its own with H-PM4 on: with the loop gone, the retire's wait for a revocation reference (8 tries, 254 ms of sleeps, then a drain wait) is the next cost a name can pay. ===== TWO MECHANISMS, EACH MEASURED ALONE WITH THE OTHER HELD ON (tests/recreated_dir_peer_mkdir.sh, dir->dir reuse, REUSE_GAP=10; per-name budget 195 ms = posix_multi's 25 s report budget over 128 names). (1) The same-type resolver reloads a shell its own reload poisoned for 200 rounds (2.4 s): switch sametype_poison_break. rdm3 (mxfs-c 8748E05ED1FFC10D220792D, no break): 10/10 laps 2425-2443 ms, P95C-SAMETYPE-WAIT rounds=201. rdm2 (D92BBDD701614A7502A4308, the release candidate, killed at the relay after lap 11): break=1 laps 1-10 25-131 ms PASS; break=0 lap 11 2427 ms. rdm4 (84F54972E2EE1B300A79815, the tree without (2)): break=0 laps 9-12 2425-2430 ms; break=1 laps 1-8 313-505 ms, every one over budget. (2) After the break, the poisoned-shell retire waits out the reference of the revocation queued for the shell behind the inode BAST workqueue's drains (H-PM3, refuted earlier only as the cause of the 2.4 s stall, which the 200 rounds dominated): switch poison_revoke_idle_skip (a shell with no dentry, no page cache and no mapping gets no revocation). pm3b on D92BBDD701614A7502A4308 with sametype_poison_break=1: skip=1 laps 1-6 PASS 24-38 ms; skip=0 laps 7-11 FAIL 492-551 ms (console tests/evidence/pm3b.console). Open until the release boards' posix_multi rows pass at 8 and 16 nodes. ===== Mechanism (1) A/B completed on the release candidate D92BBDD701614A7502A4308 (run stab, 2/disk/caw/mpath g2c test29/test30, console tests/evidence/stab.console, evidence tests/evidence/20261019T174858Z_rdm_stab): sametype_poison_break=1 laps 1-6 PASS 24-36 ms; =0 laps 7-12 FAIL 2425-2453 ms, every lap P95C-SAMETYPE-WAIT and P-RELOAD-XINCARN-POISON (reached). RESULT SUPPORTED.

defects.summary: On the 0.90.131 release build the lookup's type-flip resolver (xfs/xfs_inode.c, P95-TYPEFLIP-RELOAD) reloads a cached shell whose entry names another type; the reload finds the platter holding the new incarnation and poisons the shell (P-RELOAD-XINCARN-POISON, incarn_poison_unexposed, new in 0.90.131) instead of adopting it, and the resolver then reloads the poisoned shell for its remaining 200 rounds (a poisoned shell is never adopted in place) and fails the lookup -ESTALE (P201-TYPEFLIP-UNRESOLVED-FAIL): mkdir of a name that exists on the platter as the directory the entry names fails.
defects.evidence: dirent_type_integrity FAIL on board_8-disk-caw-direct_g8_bL2_0.90.131.log:99 (run 20261019T152054Z-g8, nodes_pass=2/8, test8 test9 test11 test12 test13 test14 each unresolved=1 failed_estale=1) and board_4-disk-caw-mpath_g4b_bL1_0.90.131.log:107 (run 20261019T142249Z-g4b, nodes_pass=1/4, test18 test19 test20 unresolved=2 failed_estale=2). g8 test8 kernlog (run_dirent_type_integrity_20261019T152054Z-g8, window from MXFS_DIRENT_WINDOW): 15:39:01 P95-TYPEFLIP-RELOAD ino=25703836 incore_ftype=1 dirent_ftype=2 name=r14 tries=6; 15:39:01 P-RELOAD-XINCARN-POISON ino=25703836 incore_gen=1029968493 disk_gen=1998383309 incore_mode=0100644 disk_mode=040755 aliases=0 inuse=0 dlm_mode=3 comm=mkdir; 15:39:04 P95B-TYPEFLIP-WAIT resolved=0 rounds=201; P201-TYPEFLIP-UNRESOLVED-FAIL ... name=r14 comm=mkdir; the same on all six failing nodes (same ino, gen, name). g4b test18: ino 23548 name=r1 and 23550 name=r2, each P95-TYPEFLIP-RELOAD, P-RELOAD-XINCARN-POISON incore_mode=0100644 disk_mode=040755, P95B resolved=0 rounds=201, P201 comm=mkdir. Also 4/disk/caw/direct (run 20261019T152054Z-g4, kernlog test4:107075 and test5:107313 at 15:40:39): P201-TYPEFLIP-UNRESOLVED-FAIL ino=4203183 incore_ftype=1 dirent_ftype=2 name=d2 comm=mkdir. The resolver loop (xfs_inode.c, the while p95w < 200 around mxfs_dlm_reload_inode) breaks only on a mode match or mode 0; the P201 relookup arm requires the platter equal to the in-core shell or contradicting the entry, and here the platter (directory) agrees with the entry, so neither fires. defects.summary: After a total storage outage of a 2-node TCP cluster (one node frozen and fenced, the other self-fenced when its storage hung), neither node can mount again without a reboot: the fenced node's rejoin mount waits two 64 s total-outage scans and is then refused because its own same-boot predecessor's record publishes its key (P-BOOT-KEY-UNCLASSIFIED, fail closed), and the survivor's remount is refused at once because its own predecessor departed dirty in the same kernel and waits for a peer to fence its key (P305-PR-SAME-BOOT-DIRTY-PREDECESSOR). Each node needs the other to fence its predecessor. Measured as an rc=124 'remount did not complete' only because the row's 45 s bound was shorter than the scans.
defects.evidence: Lap frke3, run 20261019T191249Z-g2e, build 92FBF2A83F12160EE95EA2E (D-RIG-SCST-RECONFIG-SUSPENDS-EVERY-LUN-BEHIND-A-FROZEN-GUESTS-COMMAND is the outage). board_20261019T191249Z-g2e_path_fenced_return/row.log:16 'test18 thawed at 19:16:13', :28 'ABORT: the remount of test18 (rejoin) did not complete: MXFS-RS-STATUS v=1 host=test18 rc=124'; board_2-net-mesh-mpath_path_fenced_return_chk_clean_g2e_frke3a.log:105 'BLOCK alloc_witness (node fault: test18:sync-wedged[mxfs-worker{MXFS}[msleep]...v5_boot_hb_fn...],sync{other}[super_lock]super_lock+0xe9/0x160<iterate_supers+0x5b/0xe0<ksys_sync...)'. test18's kernel log of the row: kmsg_test18_fromnode.gz (187362 lines; its uptime-to-wall mapping steps +131.126 s across the freeze at line ~187005/187066); the unmount after the thaw completed at uptime 8663.74 (P-TCP-RELEASE-POISONED for 7 AGs, DLM shutdown complete); the remount that follows is what timed out. ===== BOARD CELLS this record accounts for (run 20261019T191249Z-g2e, board_2-net-mesh-mpath_path_fenced_return_chk_clean_g2e_frke3a.log:104-106, the lap that ran through the host-wide storage loss of 19:14:14-19:15:03Z): 2/net/mesh/mpath path_fenced_return ABORTED 2026-10-19T19:19:00Z, alloc_witness BLOCKED 2026-10-19T19:19:23Z (test18 sync-wedged), chk_clean FAIL 2026-10-19T19:19:28Z (PRE-ASSERT: not mounted on test17 test18).
defects.next: Read test18's kmsg after uptime 8663.74: what the rejoin mount waited for (a dead survivor's slot, recovery, a barrier, the lease) and for how long; read the remount's own bound in tests/mpath/path_fenced_return.sh; decide whether a mount into a cluster whose only other member self-fenced is bounded by design (and then whether the bound is right) or hangs. ===== WHAT THE MOUNT WAS DOING (kmsg_test18_fromnode.gz:187328-187362): the rejoin mount began at uptime 8663.750 (TCP transport, PR key 0x4acfc087553ec557 re-registered on both paths, WE-AR held, disklock initialized, P-BOOT-STATE IDLE at 8663.809); nothing logged for 64.0 s; 8727.849 'P-BOOT-SCAN-FROZEN 2 occupied record(s) unchanged for 64041 ms -- TOTAL OUTAGE: 2 victim(s)', 'P-BOOT-SCAN-VERDICT victims=2 window_ms=62500 -- total outage, claiming', 'P-BOOT-CLAIMED ... provisional bootstrap owner; no slot, no grant, no filesystem write until RECOVERY_COMPLETE' (EOF: the row captured the log there). test17 had self-fenced and withdrawn (P163-WITHDRAW-STAMP), lease 'missed renewal 116/150' at its EOF. Harness bound: tests/mpath/lib.sh:480 pf_remount runs 'timeout 40 umount; timeout 45 mount' inside measure's 100 s ssh bound, shorter than the design's total-outage scan window (62.5 s) plus recovery; the sync on super_lock waited on this mount's superblock lock. H-RJ1 (to test): not a hang but the designed total-outage bootstrap outlasting a bound derived for a rejoin into a live cluster; open: whether the claimed bootstrap then completed recovery and mounted, and in what time. Test: the same shape (freeze V, take the survivor's storage until it self-fences, thaw V, remount V) with V's kmsg kept until the mount returns; read P-BOOT-CLAIMED -> RECOVERY_COMPLETE -> mount return. ===== ===== H-RJ1 TESTED (session 99e17361), tests/mpath/total_outage_rejoin.sh (new: freeze V, S fences V, mute both of S's paths until S closes its authority, unmute, thaw V, V remounts with its kernel log followed until the mount returns, then a bounded sync, then S rejoins), 2/net/mesh/mpath g2e (V=test18, S=test17), main tree 92FBF2A83F12160EE95EA2E, run 20261019T201525Z-tor1, evidence tests/evidence/board_20261019T201525Z-tor1_total_outage_rejoin (row.log, kmsg_test1{7,8}_fromnode.gz, boot_test18.txt, s_remount_test17.txt), console tests/evidence/tor1.console. test17 fenced test18 38 s after the freeze; test17 stopped itself 31 s after its paths were muted (7 lines). test18's rejoin: umount rc 0, then mount rc=32 after 129613 ms: P-BOOT-SCAN-FROZEN 'TOTAL OUTAGE: 2 victim(s)' at 64036 ms, P-BOOT-CLAIMED, a second P-BOOT-SCAN-FROZEN 63993 ms later, then 'P-BOOT-KEY-UNCLASSIFIED victim slot=1 node=942485699 publishes OUR key 0xb4921d4d127bc5aa -- a same-boot predecessor inside a total outage cannot be preempted by us; bootstrap refused (fail closed)', P-BOOT-ABORTED-BEFORE-SEAL, P-BOOT-MOUNT-REFUSED (dlm/v5_mount.c:5784-5794). A sync on test18 then returned rc 0. test17's remount (s_remount_test17.txt): mount rc=32 in 1037 ms, 'P305-PR-SAME-BOOT-DIRTY-PREDECESSOR slot=0 ... our previous incarnation departed dirty in this same kernel', 'TCP mount: SCSI PR register failed (-17)'. H-RJ1 CONFIRMED on its first half (not a hang: the designed total-outage bootstrap outlasted a bound derived for a live cluster) and the open question answered: the bootstrap does NOT complete; it refuses. NEXT: (1) whether a reboot of one node recovers the cluster (new boot, new key: it can preempt both victim keys and recover, after which the other node's dirty predecessor is fenced and its remount admitted) — measure it; (2) design, written before any patch: a same-boot predecessor this kernel itself unmounted has no I/O in flight (its unmount drained or failed every bio) and its key IS this boot's registration, so its death is provable locally; whether the bootstrap may classify it as fenced-by-local-proof and the dirty-predecessor remount may proceed when the bootstrap owner recovers its slice, and what in-flight-at-the-target window (SCST holds TMF-aborted commands up to 3x timeout) that proof must cover; (3) refuse at the first scan when the refusal is already decided by the own-key check, not after a second 64 s window.
defects.impact_why: Measured on the designed shape (tests/mpath/total_outage_rejoin.sh, 2/net/mesh/mpath g2e, main tree 92FBF2A83F12160EE95EA2E, tests/evidence/board_20261019T201525Z-tor1_total_outage_rejoin): the rejoin mount RETURNED (mount_rc=32 after 129613 ms, not a hang), a sync on the node right after returned rc 0, and the survivor's remount returned rc=32 in 1037 ms; no shutdown, crash or hang beyond the outage itself, which fenced both nodes by design, and no data was written by a refused mount. The defect is that the cluster cannot recover from a total outage without a node reboot, plus the 129.6 s before a refusal knowable at the first scan: recovery availability and pace, not integrity or stability.

defects.summary: tests/tooling/alloc_witness.sh fills each node's AG partition with creates until one carves a chunk, bounded by a fixed AW_FILL_MAX=8192. In multi-node mode a fully-free inode chunk is kept, not released (xfs/libxfs/xfs_ialloc.c:4789-4808, INODE-CHUNK-KEEP), so after the suite's path rows a node's partition can hold more free inodes in kept chunks than 8192: the fill ends with no carve, that rank aborts, the other rank waits for it at the rendezvous until the row's 120 s budget, and chk_clean then has no sealed witness (release=INDETERMINATE).
defects.evidence: BOARD CELLS: 2/net/mesh/mpath alloc_witness FAIL 2026-10-20T10:44:45Z (test31:BUDGET_EXHAUSTED test32:BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, run 20261020T094530Z-g2d, release chain wave bL1, build B0D2E3F5A70C96237681DF2, tests/evidence/board_2-net-mesh-mpath_g2d_bL1_0.90.131.log:127) and chk_clean FAIL 2026-10-20T10:45:13Z (:129, test31 verdict=CLEAN release=INDETERMINATE rc=0 errors=0: no trustworthy coverage witness). tests/evidence/alloc_witness/20261020T094530Z-g2d/rank2.txt (written 10:42:54Z): 'ABORT 8192 creates in the node's AG partition never carved a chunk; the free reserve could not be exhausted inside AW_FILL_MAX'; rank1.txt (10:42:37Z) FILL affine_ag=0 files=124 carved=1, SNAP S0, then nothing until the budget (10:44:48Z). Kernel logs run_alloc_witness_20261020T094530Z-g2d/kernlog_test3{1,2}.gz: P-TAUTH-PAGE-FULL 0, P-CAP-PARK 0, 'capacity=60' 0, rc=-122 0, hung task 0 (the one 'Shutting down' on test32 is the goingdown ioctl at 10:41:13, 'User initiated shutdown received', before the row: the path_peer_withdrawn row's injection). The cold audit tests/evidence/chk_clean_2node_20261020T104501Z.log (after the row, the fill's files still present: the witness removes nothing on abort): icount=39168 ifree=8410; AG 1 (rank 2's affine AG, partition = AGs with agno mod 4 == 1) count=20416 freecount=7303 over 319 inobt records, 113 of them fully free (kept chunks), AGs 5/9/13/17 64 free each: so before the fill AG 1 held about 7303 + 8192 free inodes, about 15.5k, against the fill's bound of 8192. Not D-TCP-4NODE-NOQUEUE-TRY-WAITS-9S-ON-FULL-LEDGER-PAGE-CREATES-STALL: no page filled and the fill's creates did not stall.
defects.next: After the release chain's boards end (no harness edit under a running chain): bound the fill by what the partition actually holds, read at the row's start (each partition AG's free count, plus the chunk the fill dir is in), or by the row's own budget left for its later phases, so 'never carved' means the cluster could not create, never that the bound was short; make the waiting rank stop when the other rank's file says ABORT. Then rerun alloc_witness,chk_clean on 2/net/mesh/mpath g2d on the release build, amend the two cells as the detector's (tools/criteria.py amend) with this record's evidence, and remove this record as FIXED AND VERIFIED (the lab).
defects.impact_why: No MXFS behaviour failed: the witness's fill made every one of its 8192 creates without an error and its node's partition simply held more free inodes than the fill's fixed bound; the cold audit after the row was CLEAN (errors=0).

defects.summary: On 2/net/mesh/mpath the fio_perf_vs_xfs row scored sequential write at 63% of native XFS on the same rig (threshold 70%) on the 0.90.131 build 54435C083D95EF1953F238C, where the same row on the B0D2 build earlier the same day scored 135%. The run shared the lab host's NVMe with other suites; that is a correlation, not a cause.
defects.evidence: Board tests/evidence/board_2-net-mesh-mpath_g2d_bL2_0.90.131.log (MXFS_FORCE_PREP=1 ./run.sh 2/net/mesh/mpath --group g2d, test31/test32, srcversion 54435C083D95EF1953F238C, launched 2026-10-20T14:21:23Z): fio_perf_vs_xfs FAIL 2026-10-20T14:24:12Z 'mxfs write worst 63% < 70% of xfs-baseline (/src/mxfs/.xfs_fio_baseline.net-mesh-mpath.scst-fio.json) seqW=63% seqR=146% randW=112% randR=167%'. The fio_perf row just before it PASSED (2026-10-20T14:24:11Z) with seqW=895MiB/s, host_disk[nvme0n1p2 wms_p95=304.6 wms_max=394.9 MiBs_max=938]; on B0D2 at 2026-10-20T09:50:43Z the same row read seqW=1897MiB/s with wms_p95=243.0 MiBs_max=1750, and at 03:49:56Z seqW=2078MiB/s wms_p95=111.4 MiBs_max=1993. At 14:22-14:24Z the host was also running tests/drbd_release_verify.sh on test1/test2 (its board started 14:04:09Z) and scripts/pve_full_suite.sh on pve9-5/6/7 (from 14:09Z), both writing to the same host NVMe.
defects.next: Re-run the row with nothing else on the host (the release chain's 2/net/mesh/mpath board runs it with POWER=1) and read seqW with host_disk next to it; if it is low on an idle host too, compare the build against B0D2 on one group, same fresh volume, before looking at the code. A pass on an idle host does not dispose of this: it shows only the host's share of the cost.
defects.impact_why: Pace only: fio completed its I/O on both nodes, the suite went on, no node crashed, hung or shut down, and no data check failed.

defects.summary: scripts/release.sh runs the platform build checks in 'while IFS= read -r check; do ... eval "$check"; done <<< "$checks"'; the first check (scripts/vm_kbuild_check.sh, which runs ssh) reads the loop's stdin, so the here-string's remaining lines are consumed and every later platform's build check is skipped without a word.
defects.evidence: MEASURED in the 0.90.131 release chain (tests/evidence/full_verify_0.90.131.log lines 16-59, 2026-10-20T19:52Z): one line '=== MeshXFS 0.90.131 — platform build check: scripts/vm_kbuild_check.sh pve9 6.17.2-1-pve 7.0.14-19-pve ===' and then straight to '.deb packages on the debian12 lab node'; tools/platforms.py build-checks prints seven (pve9, pve92, ubuntu2404, rhel9, ubuntu2604, debian13, debian12). Read from scripts/release.sh:102-110.
defects.next: Fix after the 0.90.131 publish (the tree must stay the chain's build until then): eval "$check" < /dev/null; then run scripts/release.sh without --publish on a scratch output dir and confirm one '=== ... platform build check' line per released platform.
defects.impact_why: A release-tooling fault: it decides which compile checks run before the packages are built, and touches neither the module, the packages nor a node; every released platform's claimed kernels still get a DKMS compile of the built package in that platform's packaged round (tests/packaged_round.sh install step, and on pve* a DKMS build for every kernel in /lib/modules).

defects.summary: tests/tcp_peer_freeze_death.sh ends by killing the victim's busy-writer loop (line 305, kill of the setsid bash's pid) but not the dd it is running, which keeps its file open on the fenced victim's mount for seconds more; full_verify's unmount of the pair then gets EBUSY (left=1), and the next step's prep (line 194, 'timeout 30 umount' with no check of the result) goes on to mkfs the LUN while that node still has the old mount, which then answers EIO.
defects.evidence: 0.90.131 release chain, platform set pve92 (tests/evidence/full_verify_0.90.131_pve92.log lines 100-125): CONFIG=2/disk/caw/direct PREP=pve92 tcp_peer_freeze_death PASS at 15:14:23 local (death at +39 s, survivor writing at +46 s), then 'pve92-2 left=1'; the 2/net/mesh/direct step's prep: 'umount: /mnt/mxfs: target is busy', mkfs_rc=0, on pve92-2 'mkdir: cannot stat /mnt/mxfs: Input/output error' mount_rc=1 transport=CAW (the old mount), FAIL 'pve92-2 not mounted after prep_cluster'. pve92-2 dmesg: the old mount's teardown (P259-DEPART-UNCLEAN, reservation conflict on its final flush, P302-PR-KEY-RETAINED-FENCE-TARGET) at 20:14:33Z, 8 s after the step began. The same sequence on pve9 and the other five sets unmounted in time (every other 'left=' line in the platform logs reads 0). HYPOTHESIS (not yet instrumented): the dd child outlives the loop's kill.
defects.next: Re-run the pve92 platform steps (STEPS=platforms PLATFORMS=pve92 tests/full_verify.sh 0.90.131). After the publish: kill the writer's process group (kill -- -PID, the loop is a setsid leader), wait for the mount to be free before returning, and make the prep at line 194 fail on a node still mounted; then the freeze test twice back to back on pve92.
defects.impact_why: A harness fault: it decides what the next platform step finds mounted and fails that step at its own preparation ('pve92-2 not mounted after prep_cluster'); the filesystem under test unmounted by itself 8 s later (pve92-2 kernel log, Unmounting Filesystem at 20:14:33Z) and no data a user wrote is involved, since the LUN reformatted under the stale mount is the test's own.
